# Check out the latest Pod with the hosts of the Long Play Series.
---
| |
Jen Palmieri and Erinn Haines, hosts of the Long Play Series, joined us to look at rising voter participation, changing political coalitions, new candidates, and the organizing infrastructure taking shape across South Carolina and other Southern states. We examine why the South is far less politically settled than national coverage often suggests, how voting rights and gerrymandering are changing the stakes, and why Democrats may have more opportunities in the region than conventional wisdom allows. If you want to understand where American politics could be heading next, the South may be the place to look. # Data Center Public Safety Committee Hearing
---
| |
Spartanburg County Council’s Public Safety Committee will host its second hearing on data centers on Wednesday, September 9, beginning at 5:30 PM in Council Chambers (366 N. Church Street). Building on the August hearing, this session will feature additional speakers and include an opportunity for public comment.

**Congratulations to my friend Amanda Richardson on being named the new Executive Director of the Spartanburg Science Center!**
---
|
---
| | As a long-time supporter of our local science center and former Board Chair, I’m thrilled to welcome Amanda to this new leadership role, and thank Mary Levens for the decade of service she brought to the Center as the former ED.
Richardson is a Wofford College graduate with a background in nonprofit management and fundraising, most recently serving as Vice President with United Way of the Piedmont.
"My family and I have loved the Science Center for years, so I couldn't be more excited to lead it into its next chapter. This is a place where kids get to touch, build, and question the world around them. It’s a joy to provide that type of hands-on exploration to as many kids as possible." - Amanda Richardson, Executive Director

| | | The commissioners of Tarrant County, Texas, voted 3-2 this week to approve **a list of polling sites for the November elections that included 92 fewer sites than the 2022 midterms** , Team. _Yes, this county is reducing the number of polling places between the primary and the general election_. The change came after commissioners heard testimony from more than 100 speakers, the majority of whom were opposed to the site cuts, during a meeting that lasted over eight hours. **The final list includes 224 sites for Election Day (down from 316) and 47 for early voting (down from 50).** _The commissioners voted along party lines_ , with Republicans supporting the reduced list, and the Democratic commissioners voting against. “ _It’s not about cost. This is about power. This is very political. This is campaigning from the dais_ ,” said commissioner Alisa Simmons. More than 1.3 million people are registered to vote in Tarrant County, which is more than live in the full states of Wyoming, Vermont, Alaska, North Dakota, South Dakota, Delaware, Rhode Island, or Montana, and about the same number of people who live in Maine or New Hampshire. clean_body: Texas Tribune: Tarrant County removes 92 polling sites ahead of November election| | | Every suppressive action these vengeful partisans take shows their true colors. For all their talk about election integrity, voter ID, and not harming eligible voters, closing legitimate polling places to make it harder to vote only has one logical end result. Attacks by opponents of voting rights on young voters, mail-in ballots, early voting, and more aren't about integrity and fairness. It's about protecting their own power at any cost and tilting the playing field before the game has even been played. = | | | | = | | | The commissioners of Tarrant County, Texas, voted 3-2 this week to approve a list of polling sites for the November elections that included 92 fewer sites than the 2022 midterms , Team. Yes, this county is reducing the number of polling places between the primary and the general election. The change came after commissioners heard testimony from more than 100 speakers, the majority of whom were opposed to the site cuts, during a meeting that lasted over eight hours. The final list includes 224 sites for Election Day (down from 316) and 47 for early voting (down from 50). The commissioners voted along party lines , with Republicans supporting the reduced list, and the Democratic commissioners voting against. “ It’s not about cost. This is about power. This is very political. This is campaigning from the dais ,” said commissioner Alisa Simmons. More than 1.3 million people are registered to vote in Tarrant County, which is more than live in the full states of Wyoming, Vermont, Alaska, North Dakota, South Dakota, Delaware, Rhode Island, or Montana, and about the same number of people who live in Maine or New Hampshire. This is voter suppression, plain and simple, by making it harder for eligible, registered voters to vote in-person by taking away their polling place. name: Roy Cooper
subject: I usually don’t speak in superlatives…
body:
If there were a way to win a U.S. Senate seat without ever asking for donations, I’d do it in a heartbeat.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1308&source=&t=1&akid=3249%2E124072%2Ex2Jzrk) | | | |
---
I don’t normally speak in superlatives, Peter, but there are two things that are impossible for me to overstate:
1) How desperate right-wing billionaires and corporate megadonors are to defeat us
2) How much I dislike asking folks for their hard-earned money
If there were a way to win a U.S. Senate seat without ever asking for donations, I’d do it in a heartbeat. However, the fact that the GOP megadonor class can spend unlimited money – _and already is_ – to try to buy North Carolina for President Trump’s handpicked candidate makes it unrealistic.
[**_So if you get the problem and are willing to help us tackle it head-on, I hope you’ll consider chipping in today. We have fewer than nine weeks left to fight back against the GOP dark money flooding our race, and we still have a ways to go to reach this week’s fundraising goal._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1308&amount=5&t=8&akid=3249%2E124072%2Ex2Jzrk)
The thing is, Big Money is why so much in Washington DC is broken nowadays. Too often, politicians opt to take the easy route: fall in line, accept massive checks – with strings attached – to win elections, and then do as they’re told to keep the cash flowing. _All the while, the voices of the working people who voted them in continue to go unheard._
**North Carolinians don’t have to settle for that.**
Those at the top are terrified of what can happen when people understand their collective power to fundamentally change the system. They’re terrified of what can happen when elections are no longer for sale.
Our people-powered campaign can overcome nearly $100 million so far in dark money and flip this seat blue for the first time since 2008 – and it will be nothing short of a political earthquake.
So while I truly loathe asking you for money, I am going to because I know that transforming our politics by taking back North Carolina – and with it, the Senate majority – is worth it.
[**_Please, Peter, will you contribute $5, or any amount you can spare, to help us get the rest of the way to this week’s fundraising goal? If we plan on winning this seat and fixing what’s broken in Washington DC, then we can’t afford to fall short._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1308&amount=5&t=9&akid=3249%2E124072%2Ex2Jzrk)

Thanks so much, Peter.
Roy Cooper

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

| Peter, I need to speak with you directly. Democrats in Florida just nominated a self-proclaimed socialist in the biggest Senate special election of 2026. Her name is Angie Nixon. She publicly and proudly joined the Democratic Socialists of America during her campaign. She’s a former “community organizer” who literally runs a bookstore called Cafe Resistance. She’s endorsed by The Squad and held one of her final rallies with Hamas superfan Rashida Tlaib. And she just defeated an incredibly well-funded Democrat with a nearly $17 million war chest by more than ten points after raising less than a million dollars. This is not a fringe candidate who stumbled into a nomination. And the socialist movement gobbling up seats all across the country can no longer be excused as some obscure “wing” of the Democratic Party. The heart and soul and energy of the Democrats is now with the socialists, and with the support of President Trump and patriots all across the nation, I’m ready to bury this twisted ideology in Florida. name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: I never planned on being in politics. Much less run for governor.
body:
But sometimes life puts a decision in front of you that you can’t ignore.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260906_4_politics.jxHxH7&refcode=em20260906-2028&amount=5&t=1&akid=2028%2E299639%2EmkrvPn)
Hi Peter, it’s Gina. I’ll be completely honest with you:
**I _never_ planned on running for Governor.** I never planned on being in politics at all.
But after a decade of Greg Abbott abandoning our schools, families, and communities, it’s obvious:**If we want change, we have to create it ourselves.**
Peter I’d like to tell you more about my story and why I’m running. [**But if you’re ready to take action now, you can chip in here to power our fight for Texas.**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260906_4_politics.jxHxH7&refcode=em20260906-2028&amount=5&t=2&akid=2028%2E299639%2EmkrvPn)
I loved my work as a civil rights and union lawyer. I fought every day for families, workers, and fairness. I represented Texans who had been pushed around or shut out, people who just wanted what they had earned: fair well-paying jobs, dignity, and a chance to build a better life. I thought I’d do that work forever.
**But sometimes life puts a decision in front of you that you can’t ignore.**
For me, that moment came the day I learned my son’s elementary school was being closed because of budget cuts. It wasn’t failing or unsafe — just “in the way” of a plan to hand schools over to private interests looking to profit off our kids' futures. Families and teachers were shaken and uncertain of what would come next, and I realized something terrifying: **No one was coming to save us.**
So I stepped up. I ran for the Austin ISD’s Board of Trustees, won, and helped block a corporate takeover of our public schools.
It taught me something powerful: **When Texans stand up, we win big battles.**
But the fight was just starting. Neighborhood schools kept closing across Texas because Republican leaders kept diverting money away from classrooms. So I made another decision I never expected to make: I ran for the Texas House.
As a state representative, I secured billions in school funding. I passed a first-of-its-kind law so Texas businesses could do well financially and do good in our communities. I delivered nearly a billion dollars in healthcare funding to Travis County. I helped organize walkouts that blocked Abbott’s voter suppression bill and fought back against his school voucher scheme.
**The same determination I’ve had my entire career is why I’m running for Governor of Texas today — to defend the Texas I grew up with and fight for every family who calls this state home.**
**Because Texas simply can’t afford another four years of Greg Abbott.**
For a decade, Abbot has sold out working families to enrich the wealthy and powerful at every step. He kicks children off Medicaid to save a few extra bucks for Big Pharma. He shuts down public schools so private interests can get rich on vouchers. He ignores families crushed by rising prices while he funnels nearly a billion of our taxpayer dollars into no-bid contracts for his donors.
With your help, I can become the next Governor of Texas. I’ve beaten Abbott before, and I’m ready to do it again. And right now, _he’s the least popular he’s ever been_ — so this is our chance.
But defeating a three-term incumbent backed by right-wing billionaire money takes real people power. It takes Texans standing up together and saying: _Enough_.
So I’m asking you directly, Peter: **[Can I count on you to pitch in $5 today and power the movement to take Texas back?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260906_4_politics.jxHxH7&refcode=em20260906-2028&amount=5&t=3&akid=2028%2E299639%2EmkrvPn)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260906_4_politics.jxHxH7&amount=5&refcode=em20260906-2028&t=22&akid=2028%2E299639%2EmkrvPn)
With gratitude,
Gina Hinojosa

Peter,
DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters this week that ICE agents can--and very likely will--be deployed to polling places if he so chooses.
Mullin said ICE will conduct operations at polling places "if there is a threat" or if "we're serving a warrant on someone that we have been actively tracking down. If we're serving a warrant we will be where we need to be."
The Secretary's comments are not reasonable and, importantly, they are not legal: federal law prohibits and imposes a possible penalty of up to 5 years in prison for federal officials who order or knowingly order "armed men" to a location where an election is taking place. The law also allows disqualification from federal office for officials who violate it.
Put very plainly: armed ICE agents cannot make arrests and conduct routine law enforcement operations at polling places while an election is taking place. Full stop.

# Happy Labor Day
Today is a day to celebrate the working men and women who keep Rhode Island and America moving. I hope you have the chance to enjoy time with family and friends and take pride in everything you do each day. Labor Day has always meant something simple to me. It is a day to say thank you to the people who show up and do the work. It is the nurse finishing a long shift, the teacher preparing tomorrow's lesson, the skilled tradesperson leaving home before sunrise, the truck driver keeping our shelves stocked, the caregiver looking after someone else's family, and the small business owner working late to make payroll. For nearly 40 years, I have been blessed to serve Rhode Island as an oral and maxillofacial surgeon and small business owner. I understand the responsibility of caring for patients, employing people, and providing for the families who depend on you. Over the years, I have tried to serve wherever I could make a difference. I volunteered through the Rite Smiles program to help children receive needed care. I testified in Washington, D.C., on health care, stood at the Rhode Island State House to defend our Second Amendment rights, and continue serving on the Board of Trustees at Assumption University. When government overreach threatened my practice and came between doctors and patients, I stood up and took the fight to federal court. I did it because leadership is not about saying the right words. It is about being willing to act when something important is at stake. | Leadership means showing up, listening, standing firm, and doing the work.
---
As we celebrate today, we should also be honest about the pressure working families are facing. Too many Rhode Islanders are doing everything right and still falling behind as the cost of groceries, housing, electricity, and health care continues to rise.
An honest day's work should provide security, dignity, and the opportunity to build a better life. That is why I am running for Congress. I will fight to lower the cost of living, reduce energy and health care costs, protect Social Security and Medicare, strengthen vocational education and apprenticeships, and give Rhode Island's small businesses room to grow.
On this Labor Day, I want to thank every Rhode Islander who gets up, goes to work, cares for others, builds something, teaches someone, creates jobs, or serves our community. Your work matters, and it deserves to be respected.
From my family to yours, have a safe and happy Labor Day. God bless Rhode Island, and God bless America.
If you believe Rhode Island needs a representative who will show up, stand his ground, and fight for working families, I am asking you to vote for me, Dr. Stephen "Doc" Skoly, for Congress.
Sincerely,
Dr. Stephen T. Skoly
Republican Candidate for Congress, Rhode Island District 2

Vote Ramona Christian for CD 5 GOP Chair
---
| | |
---
Friends,

I hope you and your family are enjoying the Labor Day Weekend.

The 5th District GOP Chair Convention will be held on Saturday, November 14.

I'm giving it my all every day because Virginia and our country face serious challenges. We need serious new leadership in the 5th.

Are you tired of the childish games that divide the Republican Party and cause us to lose even when we're right on the issues? Are you willing to do your part so we can stop the foolishness, win elections, and save our Commonwealth?

The fact that we are the only congressional district out of eleven in Virginia forced to deal with a convention right now, instead of focusing completely on the midterms including our U.S. Senate candidate Bert Mizusawa, is another in a series of failures and just one more reason why we need new leadership as Chair of the 5th Congressional District Committee.

Our district will be far more successful with Ramona Christian as Chair. Please ask friends who live in the 5th District to download, complete, and turn in the form below so they can vote at the convention. See the county deadlines below, and please share this with others.

The 5th District GOP Chair Convention is Saturday, November 14. Let's get this right.

One opened a dissent with a crude term for male genitalia. Another reversed his long-held position on birthright citizenship almost overnight.

Trump replaces three older justices on the court with younger extremists, and liberals are locked out of the Supreme Court for an entire generation. This is how Trump’s America becomes permanent.

That is what our Unpack Our Courts initiative is building. But we cannot wait until 2028 to fight. She’s proved you can make government work for everyday people — if you never give up. Rev. He’s not a stranger to struggle: he pastored striking low-wage workers, led economic empowerment forums, and built Texas’s most influential faith-based organizing hub. We need him in Congress now. Brian Poindexter (OH-7): Brian is a union ironworker who is standing toe-to-toe in the polls with Max Miller — a Trump loyalist facing allegations of domestic violence and child abuse. ## Amazon Cargo Jet Crash Kills 5 in Miami
An Amazon cargo jet [overran the runway](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGupDAMhk8TuoxCBggUKbahm223RIYY8CokKPEyYk__lHlHeI1l6bc_-fOf1_QC8hS233Cg5TVOAd_ZIzOmCQ74H8PpISAn2NDdMNO2YZq00p1Ug1RmgoXpwqmBytkVUeOzQlubvjembeu-2m3dQe0a7WBZ-w5qpdpGKzO4Z7M6mPVakS08NShTwrp_qL5Zlm5RfTtj2RWNQkcc0-NvpMA7rv6OF6bHEo_K2535zOL5S-hR6DHcZ8xcIqHHAhZ6VEMppfuXZTEUevy2k3NECps0nZEfU7kkyDtmCSwPgoMkUDpjYsmYEq13mb7IYZR5jx9Slaw73-Q95c6IRm0HkP_cxj986WX1VwAAAP__lkyLsw) at Miami International Airport just before 2 p.m. Sunday, plowing through vehicles on a nearby road and bursting into flames. At least five people were killed, and five were injured, three of them critically. The 32-year-old Boeing 767, [operated by 21 Air](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL8OmzAQxp_GbEZnx8QweOjClq4d0WGfiSuDkbkEpU9fkT5Cl9NJn_T9-f16TA9MOW3LT1zJcSzTRueRiZnqhCv-KduecSOuuFD44JyWheqkQd8lDBLshJ7TmyaDTXCRSNOtIads31vbdapvnk5hFwLNEcBYgsGDJu_VbCLYoTc2NMldfjCAVQCd6lvojfd3D303E6pghAEKiUttf5e08ZNi_pQ31daXtcnuybwf4vZD6FHo8TzPNhePWcGlCz3OryNtdBxCj1eQ0CMM17k-ZJkJD5adDIRBYmSq8t9y6bEuRX4ByBlrpUxBlhhlfW0nfiSyXBOuSWKqe6ks9NhUF_Yz5ZyOuxUGlhVT_vbk_8T7dvpvAAAA__9h-Y_F), was landing from San Juan, Puerto Rico. Rescuers worked to free the two pilots trapped in the cockpit and a person pinned under a vehicle. More than 60 fire units battled the flames and an active fuel leak for hours. [Watch the video here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuszAQwPGnMVvQcQHbDB4-fQpbqk7tiC74AFcGR-YSRJ--Sl-h81_6Df_Pa3-lEMM6vdHCTsbUr7xvkUU497TQd1rvkVaWTBP7g25hmjj3CKhP0J7A9DRIeHJfU-HdyIx8LthVxlpjmqayxez43DAgsx9bYzWBRmxHjc1Q1dQyt0VwLw9aMBVAU9kSbD0MegDb3JgqX6sa2AdJufxKYZWZx3ikJ-dySEsR3Sxy39T5n8JOYbfve3mkhzxu_OoKu21OWTaFncaPxaf_x-X9UmTn73uIMWzaqBqmhUL89eSPG54OfwIAAP__ER1yKg). About 250 flights were delayed Sunday, and disruptions are [expected into this morning](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL_GdEaLDTYULtLQXdqUaDELbGTMyTiHLl8fcckfpHvSSDN683EbbsiB4_KOG7k870Ok8wiUM6UBN_ze4z1gpJxwoemJIy8LpUGBMhI6CXZAn_lBQ43F5GYiRbogV9m2tbZpqrZYnda116azihTNqA2MHpWdZg3agumoYHf1QQe2AmiqtoS29t54aJuRsJpqUQNNnPdUfu4c80pzeO4PSqXftyK4Nef7IfSbUL1Q_XmeZRz95XHlQvUXCtV_HfKPfsXky0z6hMcqN8aNZfIRm85o0xXJTfeTQ-DDWFHDsiGH117-500Pp34CAAD__7T8fRA). The FAA and the National Transportation Safety Board are investigating. It remains unclear whether the dead were on the plane or in the vehicles it hit.
## Mail Voting Rules Head to Supreme Court
The Trump administration filed an [emergency appeal](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OozAUhZ_GdI6MwT8ULlZa0WW13ZboYl-IswYj-yaZzNOPmFeY-ugcne_7d52uEFPc1z-woaMlTzu-akIiLBNs8Jn3I8GOVGDF8IY5riuWSQqpuRi4MBN4ik-cemiCWxAldg261lhrjFKtbW7O42A6PXvtcRFGK6V71IOAQYI1dumb6M49MQjTCqFaexG29157YdWM0Iae9QJDpFwu9xx3uuGS3vmJ5eLz1iR3Izoq634xOTI5wuxPhjNjcvybU6ToK5PjggELJH5_hBU5fhDuofI5Zf-f7_jij3pUvkFMfIaUMjE5VsrlzboxBtb9bjstWyWUbYoLxyumFKs2rBfrWfr-Qj9U-HTyKwAA___tOIZl) with the Supreme Court on Sunday, asking the justices to let new Postal Service mail ballot rules take effect for November's midterms. The filing came two days after a federal judge [extended her block](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGypCAURL8GMyxAFCcg2MRsNt3QusIdh1kEC-7ozn79K98vvKyruqu7-vy5z3cIMaT1N2xo6ZHnhGeNSIRlhg3-57RHSEgFVvQfWMK6YpmVUAMXNy7MDI7CgbOGxtsHosKuQSvNOBrT93JsnlarXjsppHZG6gF13-nOaKcBbkaOKJpgrz5xE0YK0cuxFaN2bnBi7BcE6TXTAn2gXNpXDome-IiffGBpXd6aaJ9Ee2XdL6YmpqbzPFu31OvH5TM1XZKp6fX2K3L8R5h85UvM7i_fcyWIvGI5gkNO5b3tfIMQeUh8gRgzMTU1xfr9DDGGOhimxXolvsfph8wOq74CAAD__wtngls) on the rules, finding them likely unconstitutional and warning they nearly guarantee "significant disenfranchisement" of mail voters. The rules stem from President Trump's executive order on mail voting. States would give the Postal Service voter names and addresses tied to a barcode on each ballot, and carriers would deliver only to voters on the list. With [ballots already going out](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O6yAUhJ8Gd1iY-I-C4jbuctstrWM4JmQxWHBiK_v0K-cVtv40o2_m6z7fwQcf3X_YUNOa5ohnCUiEeYYNflLcA0SkDA7tGxbvHOZZCtlzobgYZjDkD5xbqKxeESXeKtTNMI7D0HXNWD100yPYdTFKqZuVoFqpZN8hKGx6YWGsvL76hBJDI0TXjLUYW2N6I8ZuQWhsy1qB1lPK9TP5SA9cwzsdmGuTtiroB9Fe2O0fkxOT03medVzMtePiTE57Cp68KUxOH3EMaMinyOT0fFmHfAnJfBdO-bXtHNc1ZeIZC2VviB-JfHR8Ax_4AiEkKrwQZOIuXSCbCJ3qhRqqrO1--hB86QfWCndlPo70x2sPLX8DAAD__yg6kSI) in some states, the justices are expected to move quickly. The challengers have until Tuesday morning to respond.
## UN Retires Map That Shrinks Africa
The United Nations General Assembly voted to [adopt a new world map](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMHOnCAUhZ8GdxhAHXHhYtrG3XTTJl2aO3BBGgSDN0OmT984r_Bv7_1ycs7357E-IMSQ_E_YcSaX14T1jEiEZYUd_uV0REhIBTzaNzyD91hWJdSNi4mLcQVD4YVrD42dHaLCrsFZjlqP4zBI3WzzhHoyWnfODMMkUCI6NND1Eq1AKacmzFeemMQohRikboXujbkZoYcngrQ96wXaQLm0f3NItKGL7_zC0pq8N3HeiI6TdXemFqaWWmu7n-n6MbVg4gaYWq5ZTC2ZNiwXtAFxG5zDgol4zSVavsNxco_ES_AbcUiWfzja8P2515KTZ2qBwu939fz-e3GsW7IJlnU_vl0WsZ6_sBxNme1RQ4zhvI2sF36HED9t6YuSX7P6HwAA__857ZNo), retiring the 457-year-old Mercator projection that shows Africa about the same size as Greenland. Africa is actually about 14 times larger. The "Correct the Map" resolution [passed 164-1](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFy6yAUheHVoM4auAYEBcVr6PzalJoruJLJIPAgYo-z-oyyhWzgO3P-j9t8w5RT2f7jTq6vdS70OjL1Tm3GHb9reWQs1BtuFN-4pG2jNgMHfeH2wqcZQ09PmiUO0a1EQNeBnJiMmSalhBnuzshFYwhCSG3FqpSNWtEiDFpCG6MZkjs9bvkkOFfCjNzIEHTgRi2EIkomOcXUaxs_ayr9Tmt-1ye1MdR9yO7e--Ng138MPAN_Hhi_yljbxsBTYeCPXtubgT9nGHhuGXghtAEjh-bi45VyToeemOTbjin_uv2POZ4OfgIAAP__bQxx5g) with six abstentions. It urges governments, schools, and tech companies to switch to the Equal Earth projection, a 2018 design that shows landmasses at their true relative sizes. [See the new map here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykj71uwyAURp8GtkQXzJ8Hhi7Z0rUjuoGLTYVNSmii9Omr9BU6fvp0jnQ-zuGMpZZ9eceN_Mgt7PS4VRqDesANf9p-rbjT6LhQeuKlLAv1IEGaA8wHsAHjKHcKCnnymUjSxMkL65y1WgvHVw_GGHFRJsc56ylPkeasUnqtrGWWvPiXD2awAkALdwSnYjQRnL4QiqSYAkpltH78bGUfK-X6bHfqx9g2Xv06xvXGpjcmT0ye6Osb64Gwj_X1M3ni3afro9RabsYyBcuGpf6x45_Jdy9_AwAA__-vjmt0). Togo led the push on behalf of African nations. _"A fair map does not change the geography of the world, it changes how we see the world,"_ the country's foreign minister said. The United States cast the lone vote against, calling the effort part of a "radical ideological project." The resolution is nonbinding, and no country is required to change its maps.

At least five people were killed, and five were injured, three of them critically. The 32-year-old Boeing 767, , was landing from San Juan, Puerto Rico. Rescuers worked to free the two pilots trapped in the cockpit and a person pinned under a vehicle. More than 60 fire units battled the flames and an active fuel leak for hours. . It remains unclear whether the dead were on the plane or in the vehicles it hit. Mail Voting Rules Head to Supreme Court The Trump administration filed an with the Supreme Court on Sunday, asking the justices to let new Postal Service mail ballot rules take effect for November's midterms. The filing came two days after a federal judge on the rules, finding them likely unconstitutional and warning they nearly guarantee "significant disenfranchisement" of mail voters. The rules stem from President Trump's executive order on mail voting. States would give the Postal Service voter names and addresses tied to a barcode on each ballot, and carriers would deliver only to voters on the list. With in some states, the justices are expected to move quickly. The challengers have until Tuesday morning to respond. UN Retires Map That Shrinks Africa The United Nations General Assembly voted to , retiring the 457-year-old Mercator projection that shows Africa about the same size as Greenland. Africa is actually about 14 times larger. The "Correct the Map" resolution with six abstentions. It urges governments, schools, and tech companies to switch to the Equal Earth projection, a 2018 design that shows landmasses at their true relative sizes. . Togo led the push on behalf of African nations. "A fair map does not change the geography of the world, it changes how we see the world," the country's foreign minister said. The United States cast the lone vote against, calling the effort part of a "radical ideological project." The resolution is nonbinding, and no country is required to change its maps. name: Chris Pappas
subject: What Labor Day means
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=8756%2E582294%2EKKnr9D ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=8756%2E582294%2EKKnr9D ]Chris Pappas for Senate

For many Labor Day isn’t a long weekend, a cookout, or a chance to catch a
big sale. For millions of people, it’s just another workday.

Today is a day to stop and thank the people all around us who all too
often go unnoticed. Unions built this country, created the strongest
middle class in the world, and continue to move our nation forward.

When we invest in and support our employees, we all do better. Living
wages, fair hours, vacation time, and access to health care can make a
world of difference for workers and their families.

The protections we rely on today — Social Security, Medicare, the 40-hour
workweek, overtime, paid sick leave protections, and safer workplaces —
didn’t happen by accident. They were hard-fought victories won by the
labor movement.

When working people have a seat at the table, our entire middle class
benefits.

That’s why I’ve fought to make sure workers have a voice in Congress. I
helped introduce the PRO Act to protect collective bargaining rights and
hold corporations accountable for violating those rights. And when the
Trump Administration stripped union rights from one million federal
workers, I got to work fighting to restore those protections.

I’m proud of my record. But there’s still a lot of work to do.

This election is a choice about who will stand with New Hampshire’s
working families.

When John Sununu was in the Senate, he opposed a proposal to raise the
federal minimum wage and argued that raising it would “price workers out
of the market.”

I couldn’t disagree more.

If you work hard, you should be able to earn a living wage, support your
family, and get ahead.

Granite Staters deserve a Senator who will stand up for their right to
organize, bargain collectively, and have a voice on the job.

There is dignity in every honest job — including bussing tables, cooking
meals, teaching kids, caring for patients, and doing the countless jobs
that keep our communities moving.

I’m honored to have the support of unions across New Hampshire, and I’ll
keep fighting alongside working families to raise wages, defend collective
bargaining, protect Social Security and Medicare, and make sure every
worker is treated with dignity and respect.

We’re always stronger when we work together toward a common goal. I’ve
seen that firsthand at my family’s restaurant, in Congress, and on this
campaign.

To everyone working today — thank you.

Wishing you and your family a safe and happy Labor Day.

Chris Pappas

P.S. The New Hampshire primary is tomorrow, and with our race now a
toss-up, this is a pivotal moment for our campaign. [ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260907_1.KjOzCB&refcode=em20260907-1&t=1003&akid=8756%2E582294%2EKKnr9D ]If you can chip in
any amount to our campaign right now, it will help put us in the strongest
position possible for the next phase ahead »

Friend of Life, Every day, women walk into PreBorn! Network Clinics carrying burdens most of us can hardly imagine. Many are frightened. Many feel alone. Nearly all of them are facing one of the most significant decisions of their lives. We believe every one of those women deserves the opportunity to slow down before making that decision. She deserves to see her baby on an ultrasound, hear the heartbeat, receive compassionate care, and encounter the hope of Jesus Christ. That's why friends of PreBorn! have stepped forward with an extraordinary commitment. They have pledged to **MATCH every gift made before September 30, up to $100,000** , because they want twice as many women to receive the care, support, and hope they so desperately need. Your gift doesn't simply become twice as large. It helps create twice as many opportunities for mothers to choose life. Twice as many opportunities to share the gospel. Twice as many opportunities for families to experience the kind of hope we've seen God provide time and time again. A gift of **$28 helps provide one life-saving ultrasound.** During this matching challenge, that same gift can help provide **two opportunities** for women to see their babies, hear the heartbeat, and receive compassionate care before it's too late. body:
It is about class solidarity.
#
This campaign is not about partisan labels or purity tests. It is about class solidarity.
**It's about thousands of people like you standing together and saying we deserve dignity and we deserve respect.**
Billionaires, and the politicians who serve them, want us divided and distracted while they loot public coffers.
That’s the fight we are in. It’s not “Left” vs. “Right” — it’s working people against the billionaire class who are rigging the system against us.
I don’t take a dime from lobbyists or seek favor with billionaires so I can fight for working class families like mine.
I’m proud that this campaign is 100% grassroots funded with an average donation of $17.

## MAGA PAC Launches $10M Senate Blitz
MAGA Inc., a super PAC aligned with President Trump, [will spend at least](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGSsyAUBeCn0Q4H0IgWFH9jl7_d0rnCNWEDwsBNdPfpd8w-wtZ35p7znY_rfAXn3Xb7DwE1HWucN9yLRyLMc4AbJDBF8FBwA8LFO_rescySy57xkXE1gyH3wrmD2uqF21HUqIUaBqWGsRX1XYuLHI0xYFtUCzeXtV0FAPTdAIDWjLXT5zs-ciUEl3xslF1EJ7rWKLEK1Zuq42gdxdzQHQkPKKv_ii_MjYmh9vpOlErV_qvkVMlp3_dmjcfpOO-VnFL0jpwplZwoP0Ni3m0PtOz0MbcZluIzFyZ4YA_cWIKD4sbeQewXzjIYZJ8QsDACD9mZWGdt0-68d6VXVcdvAZx_N6K_LvnS8icAAP__uzaMMA) $10 million in Texas' U.S. Senate race, marking its first major expenditure of the 2026 midterm cycle. Federal filings show $5 million is earmarked for digital and connected-TV ads supporting Republican nominee Ken Paxton, with another $5 million funding ads opposing Democrat nominee James Talarico. The ads argue that Talarico supports higher taxes and present Paxton's proposals as tax relief. Talarico's campaign disputed that portrayal, pointing to his support for property-tax reductions. The spending comes as recent polling shows a [competitive race](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAURb_G7ogeGBtTUGyTLttuab3Aw0EC24K3SWa-fuT8wpRXVzq65_67LTdMOW3rXyzk-B33ZaNXy8RMdSm44oG-SSiNNmS658TfL2qLAjUJsALMgp7TkxaNfXB3CFb25KSZZ2NmO8j-4SxqbREmGfyMOqA0ox0UkB5GBT4OfXInDiwYKUGBvZhwl1rqwRsZpZl8p4FC4r1e-EFMb2wxf-1Pqhe_lz67B_PRuuFPp66duuJxKpzVGSonn6lTV67_yyFKCky1NHG6ibR5gUG0g7aQtlV82AKUH0PUGKKNCDZYmAaa1WgnNUYMvq8uHK-Uc2qT6TSsBVP-TOHfXvh06icAAP__63CFGw).
## Elmore Gets 20 Years in 'Killing Fields' Case
A Galveston County jury [imposed the maximum sentence](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb_GdI7GhjC4cLENXbaJVluisRkS6xmI8Cgk7-ufyC-8-l4d3Xv-X4YLpZyW21-a2ctrWoeF95JZhLdhphs9KBYDc-GFhENO8r1zGSzYVoPTgANFSU8eGqpGH2B0pmJvsOsQO1eb6u5xcoEw1q49Q6wduy4EsJ0NeHaTDVQlf-DAARoDFtwJx2Aa09QRzWSwjaoBHpOs20nuLPyiMuX3-uTtFNe5yv4u8iiq_qNsr2xPIR4fjkzZ_t9V2X5PG19l3d7K9jMtuvAivEQetQX9ZtqK_mD1V8qHDT0lzmPRkQprU7cGOzRNtfnxsR-N0qJq4DZTyp8J8lt1T29_AgAA__84tYLr) of 20 years in prison Thursday on James Dolphs Elmore Jr., 61, following his manslaughter conviction in the 1984 death of 16-year-old Laura Miller. Prosecutors said Elmore prepared a vial of cocaine that Clyde Hedrick administered to Miller, causing her fatal overdose. Elmore's defense maintained that he was not involved. Hedrick, whom authorities suspected in several deaths, died by suicide before prosecutors could present their case against him to a grand jury. Miller's body was found in 1986 in a League City field where four young women were discovered between 1984 and 1991. Her father, Tim Miller, later [founded Texas EquuSearch](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2SpCAUhZ9GMyygWZGAYBOz3nRDC-Gi9IBYcG275-mn7FeY9NSp8_P9v093E2LYln8mgcaXz9MGZ42ACGVKZjG7sZXRVGEzCHMM-H1CnTjlPaGKUDkZi-EJkzCt0zN1irWgmRwGKQd1Y-2qrbDglHPij2RUDXxQrhczV7MXzveet0FfcVRRyRjlVHXSzUwwcbOSeSZ72wgKLmAuHa6A8DLVx3d-QulsTm3UK-Jem9vfho8NH8_z7Hx-8X7NR8W8XaaGj9evho8Pk6ASl-O-VgIx5QLkUYjPx-bIcoSIb5LMVqM5lhWhkE8f-QrxwkR8gOgqsaZCW7Tbz0uvvWwEXZIJ8bMIf0vyqflPAAAA__8b5ov_), a nonprofit that searches for missing people. name: Vera Smith
subject: Defend Our Forests: Speak Up to Keep the Travel Management Rule!
body:
Take action: Urge the U.S. Forest Service to safeguard wildlife and abandon its proposal to gut the rule.

Take action: Urge the U.S. Forest Service to safeguard wildlife and abandon its proposal to gut the rule.
                  

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5982739/38SyG9Xl)

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5982740/38SyG9Xl)

Act Now to Protect Our National Forests! (https://support.defenders.org/s/5982741/38SyG9Xl)

Defender,

Right now, motorized vehicles including off-road vehicles and dirt bikes must stay on designated roads, trails and play areas. Makes sense, right?

Well, the U.S. Forest Service is proposing the opposite – that our national forests should be broadly open to off-road vehicles and new motorized routes, even though some places might be critical habitat for wildlife or renowned for hiking, cross-country skiing or other non-motorized backcountry pursuits.

The Forest Service is revising its longstanding Travel Management Rule – the basic policy that requires motorized vehicles to stay on designated roads, trails, and areas and is critical for safeguarding wildlife. Done well, it results in dependable systems of roads and trails that provide reasonable motorized access while protecting wildlife and reducing potential conflicts with other recreational uses.

Speak out against gutting the travel management rule: Send your comment to the Forest Service today! (https://support.defenders.org/s/5982742/38SyG9Xl)

The new proposal from the Forest Service would adopt an “open unless closed” approach which presumes national forests and grasslands are broadly open for off-road vehicle travel unless individual routes or places are specifically closed. It could also force local land managers to repeatedly defend existing protections, eliminate longstanding requirements to minimize damage and conflicts, and create new pathways for expanded off-route motorized use.

This proposal comes directly on the heels of the announcement to repeal the Roadless Area Conservation Rule, which could subject 45 million acres of remote backcountry forests to road-building, logging, and other development.

The combined effect, if the rollbacks are successful, would be to strip key protections from our national forests, including some of our most valued wildlife habitat in the nation.

Our national forests need you. The Forest Service is currently taking public comments on its proposal, and it’s vital that we speak up right away!

Urge the U.S. Forest Service to scrap the proposal and retain the current Travel Management Rule! (https://support.defenders.org/s/5982743/38SyG9Xl)

Defender, thank you for taking this important action to protect the future of wildlife in America’s national forests.

Sincerely,

Vera Smith

Director National Forests & Public Lands

Defenders of Wildlife

(http://www.facebook.com/DefendersofWildlife) (http://twitter.com/defenders) (https://www.instagram.com/defendersofwildlife/?hl=en) (http://www.youtube.com/defendersofwildlife) (https://www.tiktok.com/@defendersofwildlife)

Hey y'all,
I’m reaching out to you today because we have to make sure we keep our toughest fighters in the House. Representative Shaundelle Brooks is one of those fighters. I met Shaundelle years ago after she lost her son Akilah to gun violence and she was working to pass legislation to prevent gun violence. She tried for years from the outside to get the legislature to pass legislation to prevent gun violence, when it didn’t happen, she did not quit—she decided to run for office to continue her fight to keep Tennessee safer. She is still fighting for gun violence prevention, but she is also fighting for affordable healthcare, fully funded public schools, higher wages, child care infrastructure and so much more for Tennessee’s hard working families.

name: Kirk Cameron
subject: The antidote to Drag Queen Story Hour
body:
---
| | | | | |
---
| | | | | [View in browser](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTJ9AAwAAAAAAtCc_2ZkVu8pR83syqgKA_-WaXmwaJxoLROupk7N_-eqEZ5PEd21t6xuot-Ki_0UzoxkiLc193GGBIeA31wzbkPhgko371ue2jlVrQ "View in Browser")
---
_**A Special Message from our Sponsor**_ _Please note that views expressed in this message do not necessarily reflect those of_ _Free Speech Daily_ _and do not constitute an endorsement or recommendation by Free Speech Daily_ _._
---
| BRAVE For Good We don’t have the millions behind us like the giant taxpayer-funded ALA. | | | | | Friend, If you haven’t heard about “See You at the Library Day” on Fox News or Newsmax or your other favorite news sources, **[please let me tell you why it’s so critical.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTJ9AAwAAAAAAtCc_2ZlN1YF4zgAFQ-aaGqG-G6lRtFKdDPvy1M1QTKrYzaL4GK6JR_ZUjIUmaIMMabLkSbB8pAEZ4zOUFl3Z2L0PMIz6Da0ngHfPw)** Back when you were growing up, you may remember lazy Saturdays at the library with a kind but stern librarian. She would fill your mind with classics like _Pat the Bunny_ and _The Little Engine That Could_. And eventually you got old enough to roam by yourself and discover adventures like the _Three Musketeers_ , _Treasure Island_ and _Charlotte’s Web_. **But today, all that has changed.** Instead of filling children with wholesome stories, the president of the American Library Association (ALA) says libraries should be used to address ‘systemic racism’ and elevate ‘BIPOC and GLBTQR+ writers and voices.’ Radical librarians call _Adventures of Huckleberry Finn_ and _To Kill a Mockingbird_ “racist.” They’ve stripped Laura Ingalls Wilder’s name from a prestigious book award because of her “problematic’ _Little House_ series. And they bring in men wearing full makeup, dresses, and high heels for “Drag Queen Story Hours” where books like these are read to children of all ages... _A is for Activist._ An ABC board book for “families who want their kids to grow up in a space that is unapologetic about activism, environmental justice, civil rights, LGBTQ rights, and everything else that activists believe in and fight for.” _Woke Baby._ “For all the littlest progressives, waking up to seize a new day of justice and activism. Woke babies raise their fists in the air. Woke babies cry out for justice. Woke babies grow up to change the world.” _Prince and Knight._ The “premier queer-friendly fairy tale” about a prince who marries a knight instead of a princess. And _The Hips on the Drag Queens Go Swish, Swish, Swish._ A “family-friendly celebration of drag” that encourages children to “work it.” I wish I could tell you this was only happening in places like New York City and San Francisco...but that’s just not true.
---
[](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTJ9AAwAAAAAAtCc_2ZmdRsnPQLWCNiN-kupq1iCKdt4DrdEIzMGULHZoZPNUh966hOlKZ1kLoxRaWTCY0Pt_cjKfE6FbdqgDbjlw_euZFL4pNIE6Q)
---
THIS IS A MAN leading “Drag Queen Story Hour”
---
**[That’s why parents and grandparents across the country are rising up through See You At The Library Day.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTJ9AAwAAAAAAtCc_2ZnKoE5mLzSsdKfo3qqhLNhgUkqx2mcUAH5SH_4ph4vc1jLgMgVuTUHHRyOd0--ljAy5879ehK7YU1SUHuGIl_tMuIVQREpXA)** For decades, the ultra-liberal Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and George Soros’ Open Society have spent millions radicalizing the ALA.**And as a result, a new generation of pink-haired, activist librarians have made it their mission to fill library shelves with anti-American, LGBTQ-friendly, and explicitly sexual content.** Maybe you’ve noticed all the displays at your own library celebrating Pride Month or elevating ‘the environment’ to a type of religion. Or maybe you’ve noticed the “Teen Zone” which is really meant to be a “parent-free” zone. The “Teen Zone” is filled with books like: _Rick_ about a cross-dressing Grandpa, _Melissa_ filled with graphic nudity, and _Darkstalker_ featuring gory violence and domestic abuse. **But here’s what’s really alarming.** We can’t just sit back and say, “Well, I’ll just make sure my family doesn’t go to “Drag Queen Story Hour” and we won’t check out those inappropriate books.” That may be good for your family -- for now. **But meanwhile, the ALA uses our taxpayer-funded libraries to lure in millions of _other_ children who grow up to be the very activists who are destroying our country and conservative values!** _**[I hope you see why I need your help today.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTJ9AAwAAAAAAtCc_2ZoEV_w1TkqkxgmewVREwTpDt_-O7-cbqdst6xUP583TJzouDHt4HZTsyPq7JrPToL6SgsXlBoxwI2DYxNYdKORW2SalEP7Ug) **_ My name is Kirk Cameron. Maybe you recognize me from the 1980’s family sitcom “Growing Pains” or from my work in inspirational movies like “Fireproof” and “Left Behind.” I know firsthand how dangerous it is to be indoctrinated by leftist values. Pride almost took me down as a young actor in Hollywood. But the gospel saved me. I love being an actor, but what’s far more important is being a husband, dad, grandad, and a Christian. When I saw what book publishers and libraries were doing to indoctrinate children with anti-God, anti-family, anti-America messages, I knew I had a duty to take action. So, I wrote a little book called “As You Grow” to teach children how to grow in wisdom through the fruit of the spirit. **Then I decided to go one step further and counter those awful “Drag Queen Story Hours” with _conservative Story Hours_ filled with the classic books you and I grew up with, plus new wholesome books like mine that captivate children with lessons in bravery, honesty, kindness, and patriotism.**And boy, the ALA and radical librarians didn’t like that one bit.
---
* Over 50 libraries rejected my request to host our Story Hour.

---
* The ALA helped local libraries scheme ways to keep me out including booking all the event rooms for themselves.

---
* Social media blew up with attacks: I was compared to a Nazi (that’s original), my publisher was accused of trying to “confuse and demoralize children,” supporters were described as “bored moms/busybodies who need something to feel good about,” and on and on.

---
I can’t even print most things these radicals said because it’s so vile. In the end I got two libraries to reverse course by reminding them that their censorship violated the Constitution of the United States. **And thousands of parents and grandparents brought their little ones to those “Story Hours” where we pledged allegiance to the flag, sang “God Bless America”, and read wholesome and Godly books.** It was incredible. But here’s the greatest part... From there, parents and grandparents started asking how they could host “Story Hours” of their own. And that’s how the nationwide “See You at the Library” movement was born. Last year, committed conservatives just like you booked event rooms at 201 libraries in 46 states. On the same day, across America hundreds of “Story Hours” filled children’s hearts with goodness, gratitude, and God. Conservative parents, grandparents, and patriots stood together for a very simple mission -- to reject the Left’s radical ideas and reclaim childhood innocence in America’s libraries. **[And this year, honoring America’s 250th birthday, my ambitious goal is to expand “See You at the Library Day” to reach 250,000 children.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTJ9AAwAAAAAAtCc_2ZpnlvNnwTGgcXAgqjx0LDrl_UqmgVsyHAH_H7m2aNto7R1VIcVGKWSkWnR5wMNvpqO69AlWf4Oiy1R_GJbyK6KU--KFcWiSQ)** The exact date will soon be announced. And before then, I need you! The response from parents, grandparents, and patriots who want to host “Story Hours” has been overwhelming. That’s a very good thing. But it’s going to be a big undertaking and expensive to give these volunteers the resources they need to hold “Story Hours” for 250,000 children. **[That’s why I’ve teamed with a very special non-profit called BRAVE for Good to make this year’s “See You at the Library Day” a bigger success than ever.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTJ9AAwAAAAAAtCc_2ZqBlrRcf_FGk6UeeXhGjWAC2ytypcNhYLUZvvKvyRSkgEN47EARmmuoAqgVtxYzfRJxboBxTpAw9yfw_98nGesYjfWpr7suA)** **BRAVE for Good** was started by BRAVE Books -- the small Christian publisher of my book “As You Grow” –- because so many patriots were asking how they could help “See You at the Library Day” with a tax-deductible gift. **Your sponsorship gift helps send a ‘Story Hour Kit’ to every parent, grandparent, and patriot who’s organizing a “See You at the Library” event.** The kit includes everything they need to bring your conservative values back into our public libraries: instructions for booking their library space and running their Story Hour, small American flags for little ones, fun stickers, wholesome books, Bible memory verse cards, and other specialty items. **Your sponsorship gift is the only way we can fund our “Story Hours” for 250,000 children to counter the radical leftists who’ve taken control of our libraries.** We don’t have the millions behind us like the giant taxpayer-funded ALA. **[Knowing that, please consider a sponsorship gift of $125. That’s enough to sponsor one entire ‘Story Hour Kit’ yourself.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTJ9AAwAAAAAAtCc_2ZrAtVZrAbPqtd8cWbV7M5Vtcy6zUyEM3vO8u2YKPUQBoXQfqLRCNo0Ddz80I5pGJwgQAPXuXJyZsaoP52r13oz8lTz9Sy3Vw)** Singlehandedly, you’ll be reaching 50 children with our wholesome, Godly, and patriotic message. **[Whatever you can give whether it’s $35, $125, or anything higher or lower please send in your sponsorship gift in the next 48 hours so we know how many libraries we have sponsored for this year’s “See You at the Library Day.”](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5OTJ9AAwAAAAAAtCc_2ZsZB_sgVXsfo4scnLwJQrGjTZOxsL66Oe5snau1VmJ2aVVJmba0lf0khU57uBBYQ-tFL3TDvxkVBvhv3g3c4qqAMjbXHOtAQ)**
---
| | | Thank you! God Bless You and God Bless America,**Kirk Cameron**

name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: This Labor Day, I’m fighting for workers
disclaimer_text: paid for by the American people
body:
It’s time to tax AI

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3012%2E4032634%2Eu7fTcs)
---
Every Labor Day, we celebrate the working people who built this country — and remember that the rights workers have today were won by people who organized, stood together, and demanded a fair share of America’s prosperity. Workers in mills, mines, factories, and sweatshops fought for better wages, safer workplaces, weekends, and the 40-hour workweek. Today, we’re facing another enormous economic transformation: Artificial intelligence could reshape the future of work. And once again, working people need to make sure they have a voice in what comes next. Some of the people building this technology are already warning us about where things could go. Tech executives are talking openly about AI creating a level of wealth concentration that could “break society” and create a “permanent underclass.” Those are their words. **These are mine: AI should work for working people.** American progress shouldn’t mean a small handful of Big Tech executives and investors get even richer while workers lose their jobs, wages, and economic security. **It should mean everyone has a fair shot.** [**Do you want to tax AI and really invest in people? Then this Labor Day, add your name today to show there’s strong demand for a plan like this.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-tax-ai/?source=EW_EMZ33I_HOL_ENG_20260907_F&t=8&akid=3012%2E4032634%2Eu7fTcs) | [**ADD YOUR NAME**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-tax-ai/?source=EW_EMZ33I_HOL_ENG_20260907_F&t=9&akid=3012%2E4032634%2Eu7fTcs)
---
Look, AI was built on human creativity and intelligence, years of federally funded research, and infrastructure paid for by the American people. The enormous wealth it creates shouldn’t belong only to the billionaires who own the technology.
If AI makes companies richer while putting workers at risk, those companies should pay more, and that money should go back to working people.
Right now, our tax code actually encourages companies to replace workers with AI.
That’s backward.
We should tax AI-driven wealth and use that money to make sure workers have health care if they lose their jobs, expand free college and apprenticeship programs, and guarantee good-paying jobs as technology changes the economy.
**AI should be a tool for shared prosperity — not an excuse to make billionaires richer while working people get left behind.**
That’s what Labor Day is about: Making sure working people have a fair share of America’s progress.
[**So today I’m asking you to stand with working-class people everywhere in the fight for fair rights and treatment and demand that we tax AI and invest in people.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/ew-em-tax-ai/?source=EW_EMZ33I_HOL_ENG_20260907_F&t=10&akid=3012%2E4032634%2Eu7fTcs)
Thanks for being part of this,
Elizabeth

It's Labor Day, which is a fine occasion to reflect on where we are. Many leaders are waking up to the fact that our economic system - capitalism - is becoming unduly harsh and punitive for millions of Americans.
And these critiques are coming from hard-nosed business leaders:
Ray Dalio: "Capitalism is not working for the majority of people."
Marc Benioff: "Capitalism as we have known it is dead."
Warren Buffett: "The economic system... rewards people with specialized talents in an extraordinary way that didn't exist 50 or 100 years ago. That prosperity has not trickled down to everybody who is willing to work hard."
The percentage of GDP that goes to workers is declining and has been for decades - it's trending down to 50% which would be the lowest ever. AI is going to push it below that level in the coming months as more value heads into the cloud.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9dae49b4-f1a7-4f73-b1a5-55b515100682?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
More than $3 trillion is being spent on AI which is going to soak up more and more of the value that used to go to workers. That's clear from what's happening right now to recent college graduates, almost half of whom are presently underemployed.
I was on a panel in Las Vegas this summer, and the head of an economic research non-profit said, "Well, we used to hire multiple research assistants to help research our reports, but now we don't have to because of AI. So has it thinned out our staff? Yes it has." Multiply that times a million organizations of all shapes and sizes and you get the idea.
One of the traditional counterweights and distributors of economic gains has been labor unions. However, the percentage of American workers who are members of a union has declined precipitously from over 20% in the 80s to only 10% today.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b12aade3-4efe-42cd-8be5-24818b6dbff8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Labor Day was inaugurated in 1894 by Congress as a national holiday in response to the Pullman Strikes of railroad workers that killed dozens and caused the equivalent of $3 billion worth of damage in today's dollars. Railroad workers had their wages cut and were protesting.
Today, wages might be staying level or increasing slightly, but inflation feels out of control. Grocery prices have gone up 30% in the past 10 years, gas prices are biting, and housing feels increasingly unaffordable to millions. Healthcare costs are up 76% in this same period.
At this point, socialism is becoming more and more appealing to folks. In recent polling, 58% of Democrats and about half of young Americans have a favorable view of socialism. I get it. If all I'd seen is the last 10 years I'd be angry and frustrated about the status quo too. Most corrective measures that people suggest amount to nipping at the edges.
I would summarize the challenge as this: "How do we get the American economic system working for the vast majority of its people even as AI arrives and begins decimating jobs?" The labor force participation rate is declining as you read this, to 61.4% in July, aberrantly low among industrialized countries. In Europe, it's around 75%. One-third of working-age American men are out of the workforce right now, and that problem is getting worse as young men disengage.
If you follow me, you know that my answer is to distribute the gains of technological advances quickly and broadly to the American people through a dividend or universal basic income. If you look at the numbers, it's one of the only answers that makes sense.
Today is Labor Day. Increasingly, trading our time for money is going to become less and less central to the way our economy generates value. How families get by during this time is an open question that is dying for a response. In the meantime, the anger will rise.

| Dear Activists,
This would be an excellent topic for a letter to the editor this week.
Healey and Markey are avoiding debates, including in Western Massachusetts, while mail ballots can start going out as early as September 29th.
Incumbents with failed records do not get to run out the clock! Springfield and the rest of Western Mass are not an afterthought. Voters deserve answers on a public stage, not press statements from Boston.
We need to push demanding a debate in Western Mass before thousands of ballots are already in voters' hands. If incumbents wait until after voting has begun, they are not participating in an election. They are managing one.
Some key points:
* Intentionally avoiding debates before voting starts is hiding from voters.
* Western Mass deserves answers on a public stage.
* Between Healey's cocaine-trafficking aide and the $2 billion sweetheart deal for a Boston congresswoman's husband, these politicians should face Western Massachusetts voters.

Send to your local paper and to Springfield-area outlets. Keep it short, local, and firm.
Thank you for pushing this.
Sincerely,
---
| |
---
| Amy Carnevale Chairman, Massachusetts Republican Party

I am excited to announce that Hillsdale's online teaching series, ["Supply-Side Economics and American Prosperity with Arthur Laffer,"](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckU-L2zAQxT-NfLPRH9uSDzosOCkLzZaSQ49CK02cAckSlpyl376YpvkAPc6bx_sx835dzMViwHX5sBE0lmJ88sZjcekB2z19gUtriugKxmyd4ZSPLZ1aKo11FR9gett4PXCmbqoBzaRSUvGRy-aumaOfIzDl5ajEjQkH0-fgpmGCfpIj9Q3qI49OVDJORT90N6kUU8KOijGmlCU93bO3FTpcC3ooLqWcU8CKrnRpW5qg77XmQsQb4WfCzwXcvoHv7hhC8TZAB34n_PyaD8-ec_jdHoHt6772UNNWW__wRJyLI2KmlHP2QXnPv7Nh_jGfTlfCx71GU9K-OSBizlsqGVzFdXmuInjcIxEzRIvhKTobs8VlJWL-SzcH3bzo5qA-rWmtsFYi5vfL27eT-Snb9-u1_fepZtM-f2EIWEZJeroclM6l2NT_7e-h-Z8AAAD__27CrVM) is now available to own as a DVD box set.

In this series, you will discover how taxation, regulation, money, government spending, and trade influence our decisions and impact our lives. Joined by Steve Forbes, Stephen Moore, Larry Kudlow, Amity Shlaes, Brian Domitrovic, and Larry P. Arnn, Dr. Laffer explains how supply-side economics holds the key to unleashing American prosperity once again.

But we need the support of citizens like you to promote this series to millions of Americans along with our other nationwide outreach.

Will you partner with us to promote this free online teaching series from Hillsdale College and expand other educational outreach efforts on behalf of liberty? Your tax-deductible donation will help us to enroll thousands of Americans in this series.

Jessica Berg Wilson
October 29, 1983 -- September 7, 2021

At the National September 11 Memorial Museum in New York, cut from steel that once held the World Trade Center, runs a line of Virgil:

"**NO DAY SHALL ERASE YOU FROM THE MEMORY OF TIME** "

Those words belong to the 2,977 -- mothers and fathers, sons and daughters, taken on an ordinary Tuesday for nothing more, and nothing less, than what they were: Americans.

Let them be read today beside another name, for a woman taken for nothing more, and nothing less, than what she was: a mother.

Read her name the way the names are read at the reflecting pools --

Jessica Berg Wilson.

Born in Portland, Oregon, on the last day of October, 1983, to Arthur and Gwen Berg. Class of Oregon State, 2007. An intrepid traveler who crossed oceans and came home to the one destination that mattered most: her own front door, her husband Tom, her daughters Bridget and Clara.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4698fce5-55a9-4aee-9462-0915abe2514f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Jessica with Tom, Bridget, and Clara -- the family the record says she died trying to serve.
On August 26, 2021, she rolled up her sleeve.

She did not want the shot -- her family wrote it plainly, and we honor them by believing them. She was young. She was healthy. She had no conditions, no fears for her own body, every reason to wait. But her daughters' school had decreed that no mother could serve in that classroom -- could be a Room Mom, could stand among the small desks and the five-year-olds shouting "that's Bridget's mom!" -- without proof of vaccination.

And so she weighed it, as mothers weigh everything: her conviction on one side, her daughters' faces on the other.

She chose her daughters.

**What the State Itself Confirmed**

On October 5, 2021, the government did for Jessica what it almost never does for the private dead: it confirmed her. The Washington State Department of Health and Public Health -- Seattle & King County verified that she had died of the rare clotting syndrome -- thrombosis with thrombocytopenia -- following her Johnson & Johnson vaccination. The state's own Secretary of Health, Dr. Umair A. Shah, said in a public statement:

"Sadly, this is the first such death in Washington State. We send our deepest condolences to her family and loved ones."

She was the first Washingtonian ever entered into that record. And the national countkeepers wrote her name as the fourth woman in America whose death was linked to the J&J vaccine -- out of more than eight million who received it.

Officials were right to call it rare, and they said so. But hear what rarity means at a kitchen table. The mathematics of the many say: four in eight million. The arithmetic of one says: Bridget and Clara have no mother. Both statements are true. A memorial exists for the second one.

**Eleven Days in April**

Six months before Jessica rolled up her sleeve, the federal government had already met this syndrome -- and met it in women shaped exactly like her.

On April 13, 2021, the FDA and CDC paused the Johnson & Johnson vaccine nationwide. The trigger: six cases of the same clotting-with-low-platelets syndrome, out of 6.8 million doses. All six were women, between the ages of 18 and 48. Jessica was 37 -- the exact age, the exact sex, of the six women whose blood had stopped a nation's vaccination for eleven days. When the pause lifted, the syndrome had a name, the warning had a label, and the government knew precisely what to watch for.

The mandates came anyway. And in September, a mother who wanted nothing grander than to sit in a classroom with her daughter's class became the fourth name on the list that April had already written in warning.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/72f4fb7a-0ebd-45ee-9477-5c2d7e8741f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The names in bronze at Ground Zero honor people who lost their lives for being Americans. They were not combatants in a war they enlisted for. They died on their own soil, in their own towers, on an ordinary morning -- simply because of who they were. That is why a nation reads their names aloud, year after year.

Jessica deserves her name read in that same register, because her cause was of the same order. She was not a soldier in a war she enlisted for. She died in her own city, in an ordinary autumn -- simply because of who she was. A mother. The 9/11 dead were citizens, and their citizenship was enough to claim them. Jessica was a parent, and her motherhood was enough to claim her. The mandates did not ask if she was willing to die for her children; they only asked her to prove she would show up for them. She proved it. The cost was everything.

They lost their lives for being Americans.
She lost her life for being a mother.

The wire services wrote her epitaph for her, in a headline that crossed the country:

"Seattle mother who died from blood clots got J&J vaccine to be child's 'room mom.'"

They printed her whole life in one line. It was the truest obituary of the season.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a6ae9234-f9c6-4c9c-baa7-8440b18b6967?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Every September, two beams of light rise over Lower Manhattan, as if the skyline itself refused to let go. Let another light rise over Seattle tonight. Let it stand above a classroom door she never got to walk through, and let it burn until Bridget and Clara are old enough to ask what their mother was willing to give for them.

May the answer be written where no day can erase it:

Everything.

"No day shall erase her from the memory of time."

Editorial comments expressed in this column are the sole opinion of the writer

The record: obituary as published in The Oregonian (birth, family, the "Room Mom" mandate, cause of death as written by her family); Washington DOH / Public Health -- Seattle & King County confirmations and Dr. Shah's statement (Seattle Times, KING5, KOMO, Oct. 5, 2021); King County's statement citing CDC figures (38 confirmed TTS cases per 12.5 million J&J doses as of July 8, 2021); Newsweek and The Oregonian on her being the fourth linked U.S. death among 8+ million recipients; FDA/CDC joint statements and CDC MMWR on the April 13, 2021 pause -- six cases among women 18-48, lifted eleven days later.

subject: What Do We Have to Thank Unions For?
body:
Dear Peter, Happy Labor Day, Vermont! Before hitting the road this Labor Day to join Teamsters Local 597 in Northfield, I wanted to invite you to join me in thanking a union today for the things so many of us enjoy day in and day out:
* Weekends
* Workplace safety
* Child labor laws
* Retirement security
* Paid time off

**The importance of organized labor is not hypothetical to me. It’s personal.** My husband has been a Teamster for more than 20 years, and I’ve seen firsthand how unions create dignity, stability, and opportunity for working families. Our family got through COVID, has health insurance and had time off when Jack was born because of the security that comes with being part of a union. That’s why I’m fighting so hard for [Proposal 3](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138709705/644967910/52817203?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ZmMwZTVjYi1iNWFhLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=IJmf36Eb2M7S8Ir4iLyQUjnniJIZXw_oGhzWJDhBMV8=&emci=4d85f4c4-4faa-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=6fc0e5cb-b5aa-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=43402276), a proposed amendment to our Vermont constitution that would add the right to join a union and to collectively bargain. I urge you to join me in voting “**yes** ” on this important measure this November, so workers in Vermont can be assured that, no matter the political climate, worker’s rights are protected. I’m so proud to be endorsed by the Vermont-NEA, Vermont State Employees Association, Teamsters Local 579, and the Vermont Building and Construction Trades Council. These are organizations that have spent decades standing up for working Vermonters. **In the true spirit of Labor Day, I hope you’ll join me in thanking a union member today and making a plan to vote “yes” on Proposal 3!** In solidarity, _Molly Gray_ | | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138709706/644967911/679520187?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDg5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ZmMwZTVjYi1iNWFhLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=IJmf36Eb2M7S8Ir4iLyQUjnniJIZXw_oGhzWJDhBMV8=)

friend, this Labor Day weekend, I'm proud to stand in solidarity with working men and women across Ohio and honor how the labor movement has helped build the middle class in our state.
Like many Ohioans, ties to labor unions run deep for me, and I've never forgotten the opportunity a union job gave my family. During the earliest years of my childhood, my mother was a single mom, barely out of high school, and working hard to take care of two little girls. I watched my mom work tirelessly to try to make ends meet, from taking shifts at the convenience store to cleaning homes and office buildings.
But when she finally got an opportunity to get workforce training through a local trade union, it changed the trajectory of my family's life.
---
|
---
My mom became a proud union carpenter, and for the first time, she had a stable income and benefits. She could more easily pay the bills. She bought our first home and went on to earn a college degree.
Being in a union unlocked so many opportunities for our family, and I've never forgotten this. Now, I've dedicated my career to ensuring that every family has access to the same life-changing opportunities we did.
Labor Day is a celebration of the labor movement and a reminder that the fight for fair elections and voting rights are a fundamental part of workers' rights. As your next Secretary of State, I will always stand strong for secure and accessible elections for every single Ohio worker.
In solidarity,
-- Allison

name: Abdul El-Sayed
subject: Happy Labor Day, Peter
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1001&akid=3135%2E251025%2EZCHQEa ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1002&akid=3135%2E251025%2EZCHQEa ]Abdul for US Senate

Peter, every
Labor Day, I think about the same thing.

Unions built the middle class. Unions built the 40-hour work week. Unions
gave us the weekend. Unions gave us the fact that our kids get to go to
school instead of going to work.

Unions gave us safe, secure workplaces, and unions can continue standing
up for working people if we empower them to do it.

None of that was a gift. Somebody fought for it, got called unreasonable
for asking, and kept fighting anyway.

And it's no coincidence that we have a trillionaire in this country and
lower union participation than ever before. The corporations that spit out
billionaires and now a trillionaire do everything they can to crack down
on unions in the process. Elon Musk made his money on Tesla, and every
single time the UAW tried to organize his plants, he busted them.

That's the real disease corrupting our everyday lives — not Donald Trump.
He's just the worst, loudest symptom of the disease.

The root of our issues stems from corporations and billionaires buying
control over our politics, and then using that power to pick our pockets.

Here's what I keep coming back to, though: Every single thing I listed
above was won the same way — by working people using their collective
power to stand up to those who told them to accept less.

The union hall beat the boardroom before, and we can continue expanding on
that progress so long as we stick together. That’s why today, I want to
say thank you to the people who decided this campaign was worth their
solidarity.

* The UAW endorsed us, and their members have been knocking doors,
making phone calls, and uplifting our campaign every single day.
* National Nurses United is with us too, along with Michigan AFL-CIO and
MEA, the largest public employee union representing teachers and
education professionals across our state.

In the labor movement, there's a question folks like to ask: which side
are you on?

I know my answer. Make it easier to join or form a union and stand with
workers the day they start organizing.

Mike Rogers has an answer too. He championed NAFTA, which cost Michigan
thousands of union jobs. And after he left Congress, he got $14 million
richer by working for the corporations he used to regulate. I could go on,
but you get the gist — Michigan deserves better than this.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260907-1-ak.bG5boK&amount=10&refcode=em20260907-3120&t=1004&akid=3135%2E251025%2EZCHQEa ]So if this Labor Day feels like a good moment to pitch in
$10 to support our campaign, I’d greatly appreciate it. Your
support goes straight into fueling the organizing that will win this race.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260907-1-ak.bG5boK&amount=10&refcode=em20260907-3120&t=1023&akid=3135%2E251025%2EZCHQEa ]Donate $10 ››

Solidarity forever,

Abdul

And after he left Congress, he got $14 million richer by working for the corporations he used to regulate. I could go on, but you get the gist — Michigan deserves better than this. [ ]So if this Labor Day feels like a good moment to pitch in $10 to support our campaign, I’d greatly appreciate it. Your support goes straight into fueling the organizing that will win this race. Labor Day has always meant more to me than the end of summer, Peter.

It's a day to recognize the working people who built this country — and the unions that fought for the wages, benefits, protections, and dignity on the job that too many of us take for granted today.

This is personal for me. I was raised in a union household, I'm a former member of the National Education Association, and throughout my career, I've been proud to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with organized labor here in St. Louis. And right now, that solidarity matters more than ever.

Since returning to office, President Trump has gone after the rights of working people, stripping collective bargaining protections from federal workers and making it harder for unions to organize and advocate for their members. That's not the direction our country should be headed. When working people have a seat at the table, our families are stronger, our communities are stronger, and our economy is stronger.

This Labor Day, I'm recommitting myself to that fight — to protecting the right to organize, defending collective bargaining, creating good-paying union jobs, and making sure working families have someone fighting for them in Washington. Peter,

For most of us, Labor Day probably means an extra day off spent with loved ones around a grill. 🌭🍔

But Labor Day didn’t come out of nowhere; it took _organizing_.

That’s why we have to take a moment to honor our partners in labor. Their support of Emerge’s trainings is invaluable. And they can only support us because of the membership of _each and every dues paying worker_.

These are the workers who teach our children, keep our grocery stores open, fight our fires, deliver our mail, give us healthcare, and keep us safe when we fly. To make it plain, _our society wouldn’t function without them_.
And here at Emerge, we recognize labor efforts not just happening around us, but also within us. Emerge is proud to have union representation through SEIU Local 205.

That’s why today, we salute the labor movement. Here’s to training and electing more pro-union candidates! |

Peter,

As Americans prepare to enjoy a well-deserved long weekend to celebrate Labor Day, it's important to remember the meaning of the holiday and what organized labor has done for _all_ working people in our country. For me, that starts with my family.

My Dad was a construction worker who worked hard in the hot sun every day. He did not have the opportunity to join a union, so when he got sick, he lost his health insurance. We lost everything trying to afford his medicines and hospital bills. And when I was in high school, my uncle was killed on a non-union construction site that had unsafe conditions and equipment.

**But fast-forward a generation, and I have family members who do belong to a union. And when they have gotten seriously ill, they had the healthcare and benefits they needed — to beat cancer, to provide for their families, and to thrive.**

From more reasonable work hours to safer conditions to better wages and benefits, unions have pushed to ensure that hard work is rewarded with a decent quality of life, and that all workers are treated with dignity and respect. Unions built the middle class. And they have improved conditions for all working and retired people, regardless of union membership. So if you work for a living, or ever have, you can thank organized labor for making your life better.

To my union friends, to everyone who works for a living, and to everyone who is now retired from a lifetime of work — thanks for all you’ve done for your communities and to keep America running. I wish you a much-deserved and **Happy Labor Day!**

Thank you,

Christina Bohannan

clean_body: | = Peter, As Americans prepare to enjoy a well-deserved long weekend to celebrate Labor Day, it's important to remember the meaning of the holiday and what organized labor has done for all working people in our country. For me, that starts with my family. My Dad was a construction worker who worked hard in the hot sun every day. He did not have the opportunity to join a union, so when he got sick, he lost his health insurance. We lost everything trying to afford his medicines and hospital bills. And when I was in high school, my uncle was killed on a non-union construction site that had unsafe conditions and equipment. But fast-forward a generation, and I have family members who do belong to a union. And when they have gotten seriously ill, they had the healthcare and benefits they needed — to beat cancer, to provide for their families, and to thrive. From more reasonable work hours to safer conditions to better wages and benefits, unions have pushed to ensure that hard work is rewarded with a decent quality of life, and that all workers are treated with dignity and respect. Unions built the middle class. And they have improved conditions for all working and retired people, regardless of union membership. So if you work for a living, or ever have, you can thank organized labor for making your life better. To my union friends, to everyone who works for a living, and to everyone who is now retired from a lifetime of work — thanks for all you’ve done for your communities and to keep America running. I wish you a much-deserved and Happy Labor Day! Thank you, Christina Bohannan Christina Bohannan is a mom, law professor, engineer and former state representative. Every road that connects us, every school that shapes us, and every community we call home exists because working people built it. This Labor Day, we honor every worker who built this country and every worker still fighting for the dignity, security, and opportunity their labor has earned.The weekend. The eight-hour workday. Safer workplaces. Fair wages. The right to organize.None of it was handed down by the powerful. Working people stood together and demanded it. Their courage changed America.
