Peter, America was built on a promise: if you work hard and play by the rules, you get a real shot at getting ahead. Workers built this country, and they're the backbone of Florida. That's why today, on Labor Day, I'm thinking about every hardworking Floridian who makes our communities run. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138726509/644999051/139515161?refcode=em_JJR_FR_LaborDay_090726&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDkxMjYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjg1NmEwNjEtYzJhYS1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=zrriusyVFcH4IY8eYU5SDXarTi5RadD65FQzlhh8P_8=) **I’m proud to have the endorsements of unions across our state, including the Florida AFL-CIO, the Florida Education Association (FEA), the Florida Professional Firefighters (FPF), and SEIU Florida, and more.** I've dedicated my career to fighting for them. As a workers' rights lawyer, I took wage theft cases to court. In the state Legislature, I pushed to protect workers' rights. And as Assistant Secretary of Labor under President Biden, I oversaw apprenticeship and training programs that helped people gain skills, land better jobs, and support their families. When workers don't have someone fighting for them in government, they get left behind, and that's exactly what's happening in Florida right now under an Attorney General who protects corporate interests instead of the people who do the work. This Labor Day, let's recommit to that original promise: that hard work and playing by the rules should be rewarded, not exploited. # [](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/3095?t=1&akid=5650%2E35263%2EsJaqq4)
Peter,
Wisconsin is the birthplace of the labor movement.
In this state, we fought for fair treatment, equality, and dignity of work. And as senator, I am continuing the legacy of protecting the rights workers have fought so hard for.
**Today on Labor Day, it’s a reminder of the strides the labor movement has made and the fights we still have ahead.**
Right-wing politicians in Congress have continued to attack workers’ rights. Attempts to take away protections for workers across the country are unacceptable. Assaults on the labor movement must be stopped.
I’m fighting tooth and nail in Congress to push back on any attacks on hardworking men and women, not just in Wisconsin, but across the country. I’m pushing back against any attempts to strip protections – and I’m working on moving us forward.
America’s working people are the backbone of this country — and the labor movement. They deserve for us to fight to expand protections, guarantee pensions, create more apprenticeship programs, and so much more.
I am committed to standing up for workers and fighting to make our economy stronger. Wisconsin is where the labor movement was born, and I’m going to fight to make sure we protect that legacy for generations to come.
In solidarity,
Tammy

subject: Happy Labor Day from those Behind the Curtain
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Massachusetts Democratic State Committee Massachusetts Democratic Party
body:
| | | |
---
| | | As millions of people across the country spend this Labor Day celebrating the unofficial end of summer, the members of the MassDems union wanted to do something we’ve never done before: informally introduce ourselves to you, the thousands of Democrats across Massachusetts. When people think of the Massachusetts Democratic Party, more often than not, they think of the elected officials moving our Commonwealth forward, representing the interests of millions of residents from Adams to Provincetown and all 349 communities in between. But for a small few – namely our parents, friends, and loved ones – the MassDems are six very dedicated, incredibly passionate, and undeniably crazy people who work every day to support the values and beliefs that make our Democratic Party great. We're the ones answering VoteBuilder export requests at midnight before a big door-knocking weekend, tracking down election night results until 2 a.m., driving across the Commonwealth during caucus season to help any town committee that needs an extra hand, and always showing up the next morning ready to do it all again. We're not elected officials. We don't want our names in the paper. Most days, nobody outside our eclectically decorated office has any idea what we actually do. But behind every rally, every organizing call, every town committee meeting, and every door knocked in every corner of this state, there's a small team working quietly to make sure the machinery of Massachusetts Democratic politics keeps running. So today, on a holiday built to honor the people whose labor often goes unseen, we thought it was as good a day as any to step out from behind the scenes, if only for a moment, and say hello. We won't be signing off with our names, as old habits die hard, but we wanted you to know we're here, and we're immensely grateful every single day for the chance to do this work. So from the few of us who keep the lights on, the exports running, and the caucuses staffed: happy Labor Day. Thank you for trusting us with the work behind the work. Now, if you'll excuse us, there's a Democratic Town Committee table at their local Labor Day festival somewhere that probably needs an extra hand. MassDems UnionIBEW Local 2321

[ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
Happy Labor Day!

The middle class was born right here in Michigan, and that wouldn’t be
possible without the workers and union organizers who fought for fair
wages, an eight-hour workday, and even the recent repeal of
“right-to-work” in Michigan.

I’ve seen firsthand the life-changing power a union can be, as the
granddaughter of a steelworker, the daughter of two special education
teachers, and a proud union member myself (go AFT!).

I am proud to stand with unions and their members today and every day,
because every Michigander deserves the right to organize, negotiate, and
make their voice heard in the workplace.

Michigan workers power our economy and build our communities. They deserve
a voice. That’s why I’m honored to be endorsed by union members and
organizations across Michigan, including:

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/15260?t=1001&akid=1847%2E181023%2ES9WE9q ]A collage of Labor Union logos that have endorsed Jocelyn Benson.

Michigan workers deserve a governor who will fight to lower costs, raise
wages, and make sure families can succeed, and that’s exactly what I
intend to do.

I won’t hesitate to take on anyone — no matter how powerful — who gets in
the way of that mission. Together, we can build a Michigan where everyone
can afford to live and thrive, but I need your help. [ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/15260?t=1002&akid=1847%2E181023%2ES9WE9q ]If you’re ready to

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138729731/645009995/-3547583?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjc2MDc2N2RiLWM1YWEtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMjI0ODJhOTMzYiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=DokLsh3yIasW1Yt45RrKdYy2gXFZ3_2D2mNw6Qj21iE=&emci=f569aeaf-b0a7-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=760767db-c5aa-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=8431045)

Happy Labor Day, Peter! It’s the only official holiday that honors the workers and labor unions that, to put it one way, make America great. Three-day weekends like this — heck, weekends in general — wouldn’t exist without them. **It’s also a timely reminder that the cause of organized labor is inextricably linked to our cause of defending democracy and fair representation.** Progress for working families relies on the will of the people being heard. It’s no coincidence that the forces that want to make it harder to vote are the same folks who want to make it harder for workers to form unions. My grandfather was a proud member of the United Auto Workers, and I was taught from an early age the value of workers coming together to advocate for their value and their families’ futures. And I’ll never forget when the Michigan legislature passed so-called “right to work” legislation to undercut my home state’s strong pro-worker legacy. For years, the state had a reputation for having some of the most gerrymandered political maps in the country. Despite Democrats routinely winning more votes across the state, Republicans held majorities in the state legislature, thanks to rampant map manipulation. Ultimately leading to anti-worker legislation getting passed. Then, everything changed. Thanks in part to the fair maps movement, voters in 2018 passed a ballot measure to reform the redistricting process — taking it away from the legislature and handing it over to an independent commission of citizens. The very first map produced by this new, fair process resulted in the first legislative power shift in 40 years. That Democratic legislature repealed Michigan’s so-called “right to work” law, which had been hurting working families — _the first state in 58 years to roll back that kind of anti-union law!_ It’s a powerful reminder of why we do this work. **The only way to ensure our elected officials reflect the true will of the people is to enact redistricting reforms and strengthen voting rights.** We know we’ve spent too much of the last year going in the wrong direction — as we witness a full-on redistricting crisis across America. It has to end here and now. That means mobilizing voters ahead of the midterm elections, electing pro-democracy champions in the most critical state-level races, and building organizing power in states across the country. **Ending map manipulation could profoundly impact future progress — thank you for being part of this grassroots movement that will make it happen.** Brianna Shamsuddoha
Director of Mobilization

name: Ken Martin (via DNC HQ)
subject: This Labor Day
body:
---
Hi Derek, it’s Ken Martin. I’m reaching out to share a few reflections on Labor Day. Today, we reflect on the labor movement’s impact on our country, and the work we still have ahead of us for every worker to be treated with respect and dignity. This fight is personal for me: I come from a union family, I carried a union card, and I led the Minnesota Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party for 14 years prior to joining the DNC as Chair. The fight for workers has been the fight of my lifetime. **Right now, Donald Trump and his Republican allies are attacking organized labor and putting workers in harm’s way by rolling** back key safety protections and regulations for workers nationwide, reducing the minimum wage for federal contractors, and stripping collective bargaining rights from federal employees in unions. **Derek, Donald Trump’s goal is clear: strip rights from American workers while lining his pockets and profiting off of the presidency.** The fight to defend working Americans against Trump and the ultra-wealthy elites has never been more dire. There has never been a more important moment to take a stand. That’s why I’m proud to work every day to elect more Democrats — the party of champions for workers. This year we have the chance to put a check on the Trump administration’s anti-worker agenda at the ballot box. It’s an honor to serve the Democratic Party as DNC Chair, and to continue fighting for all of you, this Labor Day and every day. Thank you, Ken Ken Martin
Chair
Democratic National Committee

> It is deeply saddening to see how quickly memory can fade. On Tuesday, September 11, 2001, America suffered a terrorist attack that killed over 3000 innocent people, scarring countless thousands more, and changed the trajectory of our nation. The victims were not abstractions; they were parents, children, police officers, fire fighters, office workers, travelers, and strangers in a foreign land that never had a chance to say goodbye to loved ones. Their lives deserve more than an annual ceremony or a few moments of silence. They deserve a country of grateful citizens that remembers the lessons learned as well as the perpetrators of that fateful day.
> We should remember the courage displayed in the face of unimaginable terror. First responders and ordinary citizens alike, ran towards the danger, while many rightfully fled. We should remember the families that anxiously waited for phone calls that never came, and the souls that were never heard from again. Communities across the country mourned together; and for a brief period, Americans recognized that national unity was not just a catchphrase, but a moral responsibility. The type of unity that doesn't require additional tragedies as a reminder.
> | [](https://substack.com/redirect/003a3e52-95f6-4b56-96cd-d7582d92c0e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
> ---|---|---
> Yet here we are twenty-five years later, and far too many people have allowed that horrific day to fade into the background. A dark footnote barely mentioned in history books; or perhaps a solemn anniversary post on social media before everyone returns to ordinary life. That forgetting is not harmless, it diminishes the victims, insults the survivors, and abandons the lessons bought at an unbearable cost.
> On that day, Islamic terrorists hijacked four U.S. commercial airplanes. They crashed two of them into both towers of the World Trade Center in New York City, another struck the Pentagon, and the heroic passengers aboard United Airlines Flight 93 forced the crash of the fourth plane into a field in Shanksville Pennsylvania before it could reach its intended target, the U.S. Capitol; sacrificing their lives so that others may live. I get goosebumps every time I hear the story of courage and sacrifice aboard U.S. Airlines Flight 93 that fateful day. The words "Let's roll" will always have its own special meaning in American history.
> But these attacks were not just an organized act of mass murder by Islamic extremists, they were a blatant attack on the American way of life, which is something we must never forget. To some this may sound controversial, but it is indeed a fact.
> Yet, public conversations become so desperate to avoid offending Muslim culture that it blurs responsibility into vague phrases about violence and zealotry. Evil does not become less evil by clouding the truth; it only emboldens it. Islamic extremists planned, financed, and executed a barbaric attack against innocent civilians. They should be identified plainly, condemned unequivocally, and never romanticized, excused, or transformed into symbols of tyrannical rebellion.
> Americans have every right to remain angry about the tragedy of 9/11 and must remain vigilant to prevent it from ever happening again. It is perfectly legitimate to demand that government agencies identify threats, enforce immigration laws, secure the nation's borders, and investigate extremist networks, both foreign and domestic.
> The Islamic terrorists who attacked the United States that day wanted to instill fear, with the hopes of destroying our nations will. We learned quickly that our gracious welcome mat and generosity were used as weapons against us. Careless procedures at airports coupled with virtue signaling and lax immigration policies created the perfect storm for the unthinkable to take place. It's important we assign the appropriate blame to the actual perpetrators though. Islamic extremism is the number one threat to America's security and should always be treated as such.
> Going forward, education is essential for the next generation to gain a clear-eyed understanding of what actually took place on 9/11. Young people born after 2001 should not be expected to interpret September 11th through random AI internet clips or distorted political viewpoints. They should learn what happened, why it happened, who carried out this barbaric act, and the continuous threat we face from radical Islam. They should study the courage and compassion that emerged that day, as an entire population came together as one grieving family.
> Those lost that day should not be dragged into ideological arguments or used as props. Their lives were real, their grieving families are real, and their suffering was never meant to be used as a rhetorical tool to be wielded on anniversaries. Honest remembrance requires holding these two simple truths at once; Islamic terrorists committed an atrocious act against innocent civilians, and they want nothing more than to do it again.
> Our nations legacy is shaped by what it chooses to preserve. Hope remains possible because remembrance produces an enduring responsibility. We must teach future generations to recognize propaganda, resist dehumanization, and reject the mantra of moral equivalency perpetrated by those same bad actors. By doing so, we pay eternal homage to the survivors and to the families of victims lost on 9/11.
> | [](https://substack.com/redirect/8e79deb9-dc05-42d1-8da2-1dee20134d7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

First responders and ordinary citizens alike, ran towards the danger | | | Sep 7 | | | | | | | | | | | | It is deeply saddening to see how quickly memory can fade. On Tuesday, September 11, 2001, America suffered a terrorist attack that killed over 3000 innocent people, scarring countless thousands more, and changed the trajectory of our nation. The victims were not abstractions; they were parents, children, police officers, fire fighters, office workers, travelers, and strangers in a foreign land that never had a chance to say goodbye to loved ones. Their lives deserve more than an annual ceremony or a few moments of silence. They deserve a country of grateful citizens that remembers the lessons learned as well as the perpetrators of that fateful day. We should remember the courage displayed in the face of unimaginable terror. First responders and ordinary citizens alike, ran towards the danger, while many rightfully fled. We should remember the families that anxiously waited for phone calls that never came, and the souls that were never heard from again. Communities across the country mourned together; and for a brief period, Americans recognized that national unity was not just a catchphrase, but a moral responsibility. The type of unity that doesn't require additional tragedies as a reminder. | | ---|---|--- Yet here we are twenty-five years later, and far too many people have allowed that horrific day to fade into the background. A dark footnote barely mentioned in history books; or perhaps a solemn anniversary post on social media before everyone returns to ordinary life. That forgetting is not harmless, it diminishes the victims, insults the survivors, and abandons the lessons bought at an unbearable cost. On that day, Islamic terrorists hijacked four U.S. commercial airplanes. They crashed two of them into both towers of the World Trade Center in New York City, another struck the Pentagon, and the heroic passengers aboard United Airlines Flight 93 forced the crash of the fourth plane into a field in Shanksville Pennsylvania before it could reach its intended target, the U.S. Capitol; sacrificing their lives so that others may live. I get goosebumps every time I hear the story of courage and sacrifice aboard U.S. Airlines Flight 93 that fateful day. The words "Let's roll" will always have its own special meaning in American history. But these attacks were not just an organized act of mass murder by Islamic extremists, they were a blatant attack on the American way of life, which is something we must never forget. To some this may sound controversial, but it is indeed a fact. Yet, public conversations become so desperate to avoid offending Muslim culture that it blurs responsibility into vague phrases about violence and zealotry. Evil does not become less evil by clouding the truth; it only emboldens it. Islamic extremists planned, financed, and executed a barbaric attack against innocent civilians. They should be identified plainly, condemned unequivocally, and never romanticized, excused, or transformed into symbols of tyrannical rebellion. Americans have every right to remain angry about the tragedy of 9/11 and must remain vigilant to prevent it from ever happening again. It is perfectly legitimate to demand that government agencies identify threats, enforce immigration laws, secure the nation's borders, and investigate extremist networks, both foreign and domestic. The Islamic terrorists who attacked the United States that day wanted to instill fear, with the hopes of destroying our nations will. We learned quickly that our gracious welcome mat and generosity were used as weapons against us. Careless procedures at airports coupled with virtue signaling and lax immigration policies created the perfect storm for the unthinkable to take place. It's important we assign the appropriate blame to the actual perpetrators though. Islamic extremism is the number one threat to America's security and should always be treated as such. Going forward, education is essential for the next generation to gain a clear-eyed understanding of what actually took place on 9/11. Young people born after 2001 should not be expected to interpret September 11th through random AI internet clips or distorted political viewpoints. They should learn what happened, why it happened, who carried out this barbaric act, and the continuous threat we face from radical Islam. They should study the courage and compassion that emerged that day, as an entire population came together as one grieving family. Those lost that day should not be dragged into ideological arguments or used as props. Their lives were real, their grieving families are real, and their suffering was never meant to be used as a rhetorical tool to be wielded on anniversaries. Honest remembrance requires holding these two simple truths at once; Islamic terrorists committed an atrocious act against innocent civilians, and they want nothing more than to do it again. Our nations legacy is shaped by what it chooses to preserve. Hope remains possible because remembrance produces an enduring responsibility. We must teach future generations to recognize propaganda, resist dehumanization, and reject the mantra of moral equivalency perpetrated by those same bad actors. By doing so, we pay eternal homage to the survivors and to the families of victims lost on 9/11. | | ---|---|--- Editorial comments expressed in this column are the sole opinion of the writer Thanks for reading! From our Ashtabula kickoff to the fight for Ohio communities, here’s what’s happening.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/6P5TLEnJpof?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Dear friend,
**The momentum is building.** Across our district, neighbors are coming together, sharing their concerns, and joining a campaign focused on listening, solving problems, and creating a better future for Ohio. Here’s what’s happening this week — and how you can be part of it.
---
|
---
|
---
| |
# The Great Geauga County Fair
---
| |
Labor Day weekend is almost here, and I’m looking forward to spending it with people across Ohio’s 14th District.
This Saturday, I’ll be at the **Great Geauga County Fair** , one of Ohio’s great traditions and the state’s oldest continuous county fair. For generations, the fair has brought together families, farmers, small businesses, and neighbors from across Geauga County and beyond.
I hope you’ll stop by, say hello, and introduce yourself. **I want to hear what’s happening in your community, what’s working, and where you need help.**

---
|
---
|
---
| |
# Ashtabula Local Food Festival
---
| | Maria will be walking around the Harbor this Sunday, enjoying the local food, and talking with people along the way.
Join her in exploring the restaurants, wineries, breweries, and shops that make Historic Ashtabula Harbor such a special part of our community.
If you see Maria, stop and say hello! She’d love to meet you, hear what’s on your mind, and talk about what matters to you and your community.
---
|
---
| |
# Election Matters
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/d8W4U8Sr5jP?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
| | **Ashtabula County Campaign Kickoff** Maria Jukic officially kicked off her Ashtabula County campaign with a community event at the Jefferson Community Recreation Center, where she shared her vision for Ohio’s 14th Congressional District and discussed issues including affordability, healthcare, artificial intelligence, data centers, and restoring trust in government.During the event, Maria emphasized her commitment to representing everyday Americans rather than special interests.

The event also highlighted Maria’s concerns about the rapid expansion of AI data centers and the need for responsible regulation that protects local communities while encouraging innovation.**Read the full story in the Star Beacon** :
[https://www.starbeacon.com/news/congressional-candidate-stops-in-jefferson/article_8bb63314-ce09-474b-8499-d594c3b3c53b.html](https://us.list-manage.com/j2cPFLxk1Ve?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)

---
|
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/RBdfZPk0l44?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
| |
Maria joined healthcare advocates, local leaders, and community members in Warren to support efforts to restore local hospital services for Trumbull County residents.During the event, Maria spoke about the importance of protecting access to quality healthcare and ensuring families don’t have to travel farther or wait longer to receive the care they need. Drawing on her 24 years of healthcare experience, she emphasized that access to healthcare is a community issue that affects patients, families, workers, and local economies.WKBN interviewed Maria during the rally and highlighted the community’s call to reopen Trumbull County Hospital.
**“The government needs to do something to help address communities like this that don’t have enough access to healthcare services.”**
– Maria Jukic**Watch/read the full WKBN story:**
[ https://www.wkbn.com/news/local-news/warren-news/organizations-advocate-for-reopening-of-trumbull-county-hospital/](https://us.list-manage.com/HrtbjBCFVIy?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
---
|
---
| |
# Calling all donors.

**Any amount helps.** $10, $25, $50 — every contribution helps put Maria Jukic on the field and keep this campaign moving forward.
---
|
---

Join our booster club 💙

should you choose to accept it.**
Forward this email to five people who should know about our campaign.
That's it. No skydiving required.
Every conversation starts somewhere. Let it start with you.

name: Gretchen Whitmer
subject: On Labor Day
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Fight Like Hell PAC
body:
Today, I'm thinking about the workers |
#
---
Folks, Labor Day has always meant something special here in Michigan. Our state was built by people who showed up, worked hard, organized, and fought for a better life for their families. We put the world on wheels and created the middle class through hard work, grit, and looking out for one another. That history still shapes who we are today. Right now, I’m hearing from working people who are worried about rising prices, their jobs, and what all the uncertainty in our economy means for their families. That’s why I’ve been so outspoken about reckless tariffs and trade policies that put American workers in the crosshairs. That’s especially true in Michigan, where our economy is deeply connected to Canada. I’ve joked that Canadians are like the in-laws you actually like. But there’s a serious point behind it — our workers, businesses, and communities have spent generations building things together. When Washington throws that relationship into chaos, working families are the ones who end up paying the price. Michigan’s own analysis has found higher food prices, weaker exports to Canada, and added costs for businesses and consumers. So on this Labor Day, my promise to you is that **I will always fight for working people** , in Michigan, and anywhere else families are working hard to build a good life. name: Rep. Ilhan Omar
subject: The working class is worth fighting for
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ILHAN FOR CONGRESS
body:
Today is a day to recognize and celebrate the incredible contributions of working Americans
# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2454%2E791427%2EeUl0uq)
Friend, happy Labor Day.
Today is a day to recognize and celebrate the incredible contributions of working Americans and the achievements of the labor movement throughout history.
But today is also a day to recognize the gravity of the current moment. Right now, the working class is under devastating and sustained attacks by the billionaire class and their far-right allies.
That’s because after bankrolling Trump’s campaign, corporate interests are getting everything they’ve ever dreamed of, at the expense of the rest of us.
In just the last year and a half, we’ve seen Elon Musk run wild, slashing critical federal programs, massive tax cuts for billionaires paid for by defunding Medicaid, millions of families kicked off of SNAP food assistance, presidential pardons for wealthy financial criminals, and corrupt, self-enriching deals being made across Trump’s government.
But we must also recognize that our government’s failure to deliver for the working class started well before Trump, too.
Millions have suffered without health insurance, or gone broke paying for it, while every other developed nation has universal coverage. Worker protections have eroded and big companies have been emboldened to cut corners, steal wages, and underpay. The federal minimum wage hasn’t been raised since 2009 — it remains just $7.25 an hour. And meanwhile, the cost of everything from rent to groceries to childcare has skyrocketed out of control.
**If we want to fix this broken system, we must be unafraid to take on the immense power of the billionaire class and fight for transformative ideas.**
We have a lot of work to do, but our vision of the future is worth fighting for: Healthcare for all, a roof over every head, a quality education for every child from pre-K to college, a good-paying job for everyone who can work, and an economy where everyone can afford not just the basics, but a great life.
The billionaires may have the money, but we have the numbers. We can and must demand change, organize for it, and deliver.
In solidarity with every working person in America,
— Rep. Ilhan Omar
* * *

**Hey there! Before you swipe or scroll away...**
Ilhan Omar has always been on the leading edge of the fight for the working class in Congress, despite the pushback of corporate interests. She needs a big team behind her to keep up that fight, especially as we approach an all-important midterm election. It is deeply saddening to see how quickly memory can fade. On Tuesday, September 11, 2001, America suffered a terrorist attack that killed over 3000 innocent people, scarring countless thousands more, and changed the trajectory of our nation. The victims were not abstractions; they were parents, children, police officers, fire fighters, office workers, travelers, and strangers in a foreign land that never had a chance to say goodbye to loved ones. Their lives deserve more than an annual ceremony or a few moments of silence. They deserve a country of grateful citizens that remembers the lessons learned as well as the perpetrators of that fateful day.
We should remember the courage displayed in the face of unimaginable terror. First responders and ordinary citizens alike, ran towards the danger, while many rightfully fled. We should remember the families that anxiously waited for phone calls that never came, and the souls that were never heard from again. Communities across the country mourned together; and for a brief period, Americans recognized that national unity was not just a catchphrase, but a moral responsibility. The type of unity that doesn't require additional tragedies as a reminder.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4216b6ba-9e27-41d3-a3d8-c8cf97fbb784?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Yet here we are twenty-five years later, and far too many people have allowed that horrific day to fade into the background. A dark footnote barely mentioned in history books; or perhaps a solemn anniversary post on social media before everyone returns to ordinary life. That forgetting is not harmless, it diminishes the victims, insults the survivors, and abandons the lessons bought at an unbearable cost.
On that day, Islamic terrorists hijacked four U.S. commercial airplanes. They crashed two of them into both towers of the World Trade Center in New York City, another struck the Pentagon, and the heroic passengers aboard United Airlines Flight 93 forced the crash of the fourth plane into a field in Shanksville Pennsylvania before it could reach its intended target, the U.S. Capitol; sacrificing their lives so that others may live. I get goosebumps every time I hear the story of courage and sacrifice aboard U.S. Airlines Flight 93 that fateful day. The words "Let's roll" will always have its own special meaning in American history.
But these attacks were not just an organized act of mass murder by Islamic extremists, they were a blatant attack on the American way of life, which is something we must never forget. To some this may sound controversial, but it is indeed a fact.
Yet, public conversations become so desperate to avoid offending Muslim culture that it blurs responsibility into vague phrases about violence and zealotry. Evil does not become less evil by clouding the truth; it only emboldens it. Islamic extremists planned, financed, and executed a barbaric attack against innocent civilians. They should be identified plainly, condemned unequivocally, and never romanticized, excused, or transformed into symbols of tyrannical rebellion.
Americans have every right to remain angry about the tragedy of 9/11 and must remain vigilant to prevent it from ever happening again. It is perfectly legitimate to demand that government agencies identify threats, enforce immigration laws, secure the nation's borders, and investigate extremist networks, both foreign and domestic.
The Islamic terrorists who attacked the United States that day wanted to instill fear, with the hopes of destroying our nations will. We learned quickly that our gracious welcome mat and generosity were used as weapons against us. Careless procedures at airports coupled with virtue signaling and lax immigration policies created the perfect storm for the unthinkable to take place. It's important we assign the appropriate blame to the actual perpetrators though. Islamic extremism is the number one threat to America's security and should always be treated as such.
Going forward, education is essential for the next generation to gain a clear-eyed understanding of what actually took place on 9/11. Young people born after 2001 should not be expected to interpret September 11th through random AI internet clips or distorted political viewpoints. They should learn what happened, why it happened, who carried out this barbaric act, and the continuous threat we face from radical Islam. They should study the courage and compassion that emerged that day, as an entire population came together as one grieving family.
Those lost that day should not be dragged into ideological arguments or used as props. Their lives were real, their grieving families are real, and their suffering was never meant to be used as a rhetorical tool to be wielded on anniversaries. Honest remembrance requires holding these two simple truths at once; Islamic terrorists committed an atrocious act against innocent civilians, and they want nothing more than to do it again.
Our nations legacy is shaped by what it chooses to preserve. Hope remains possible because remembrance produces an enduring responsibility. We must teach future generations to recognize propaganda, resist dehumanization, and reject the mantra of moral equivalency perpetrated by those same bad actors. By doing so, we pay eternal homage to the survivors and to the families of victims lost on 9/11.

Remember the courage displayed in the face of unimaginable terror. | | | Sep 7 | | | | | | | | | | | | It is deeply saddening to see how quickly memory can fade. On Tuesday, September 11, 2001, America suffered a terrorist attack that killed over 3000 innocent people, scarring countless thousands more, and changed the trajectory of our nation. The victims were not abstractions; they were parents, children, police officers, fire fighters, office workers, travelers, and strangers in a foreign land that never had a chance to say goodbye to loved ones. Their lives deserve more than an annual ceremony or a few moments of silence. They deserve a country of grateful citizens that remembers the lessons learned as well as the perpetrators of that fateful day. We should remember the courage displayed in the face of unimaginable terror. First responders and ordinary citizens alike, ran towards the danger, while many rightfully fled. We should remember the families that anxiously waited for phone calls that never came, and the souls that were never heard from again. Communities across the country mourned together; and for a brief period, Americans recognized that national unity was not just a catchphrase, but a moral responsibility. The type of unity that doesn't require additional tragedies as a reminder. | | ---|---|--- Yet here we are twenty-five years later, and far too many people have allowed that horrific day to fade into the background. A dark footnote barely mentioned in history books; or perhaps a solemn anniversary post on social media before everyone returns to ordinary life. That forgetting is not harmless, it diminishes the victims, insults the survivors, and abandons the lessons bought at an unbearable cost. On that day, Islamic terrorists hijacked four U.S. commercial airplanes. They crashed two of them into both towers of the World Trade Center in New York City, another struck the Pentagon, and the heroic passengers aboard United Airlines Flight 93 forced the crash of the fourth plane into a field in Shanksville Pennsylvania before it could reach its intended target, the U.S. Capitol; sacrificing their lives so that others may live. I get goosebumps every time I hear the story of courage and sacrifice aboard U.S. Airlines Flight 93 that fateful day. The words "Let's roll" will always have its own special meaning in American history. But these attacks were not just an organized act of mass murder by Islamic extremists, they were a blatant attack on the American way of life, which is something we must never forget. To some this may sound controversial, but it is indeed a fact. Yet, public conversations become so desperate to avoid offending Muslim culture that it blurs responsibility into vague phrases about violence and zealotry. Evil does not become less evil by clouding the truth; it only emboldens it. Islamic extremists planned, financed, and executed a barbaric attack against innocent civilians. They should be identified plainly, condemned unequivocally, and never romanticized, excused, or transformed into symbols of tyrannical rebellion. Americans have every right to remain angry about the tragedy of 9/11 and must remain vigilant to prevent it from ever happening again. It is perfectly legitimate to demand that government agencies identify threats, enforce immigration laws, secure the nation's borders, and investigate extremist networks, both foreign and domestic. The Islamic terrorists who attacked the United States that day wanted to instill fear, with the hopes of destroying our nations will. We learned quickly that our gracious welcome mat and generosity were used as weapons against us. Careless procedures at airports coupled with virtue signaling and lax immigration policies created the perfect storm for the unthinkable to take place. It's important we assign the appropriate blame to the actual perpetrators though. Islamic extremism is the number one threat to America's security and should always be treated as such. Going forward, education is essential for the next generation to gain a clear-eyed understanding of what actually took place on 9/11. Young people born after 2001 should not be expected to interpret September 11th through random AI internet clips or distorted political viewpoints. They should learn what happened, why it happened, who carried out this barbaric act, and the continuous threat we face from radical Islam. They should study the courage and compassion that emerged that day, as an entire population came together as one grieving family. Those lost that day should not be dragged into ideological arguments or used as props. Their lives were real, their grieving families are real, and their suffering was never meant to be used as a rhetorical tool to be wielded on anniversaries. Honest remembrance requires holding these two simple truths at once; Islamic terrorists committed an atrocious act against innocent civilians, and they want nothing more than to do it again. Our nations legacy is shaped by what it chooses to preserve. Hope remains possible because remembrance produces an enduring responsibility. We must teach future generations to recognize propaganda, resist dehumanization, and reject the mantra of moral equivalency perpetrated by those same bad actors. Living in the anthracite coal region, you can't celebrate Labor Day without thinking about mine workers, and the long, hard history of their fight for rights.
My great-great-great grandfather fled Ireland in the 1800s and moved to Foster Township, where his sons went to work in the coal mines.
Two hundred years later, growing up a few miles south of those mines, I learned the stories of the miners who stood together for good pay and safe working conditions, only to be met with silence or even violence.
Coal powered our nation's growth. But the communities here paid a brutal price - [mine](https://substack.com/redirect/e2c1ba92-7b93-4926-95db-62602ca502d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [disasters](https://substack.com/redirect/35403d12-76d9-45bf-955b-35c557f15ae0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), worker strikes, and even [massacres](https://substack.com/redirect/72d069f8-ff04-4bc7-b75f-9a86c17581c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Not to mention black lung disease.
It's why mine workers were [some of the first to unionize](https://substack.com/redirect/1fde2281-42ef-46e1-8385-3907322fc10c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the country. They organized and fought for child labor laws, workplace safety, and 8-hour workdays.
The fight of the coal miners continues today. For the past two years, the United States government has [refused to protect miners](https://substack.com/redirect/ead9b9bf-ec55-4fb7-a0c9-a03ec6eeddb5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from a surge in lung disease from killer dust hurting workers in our mines.
In other words - our fight continues.
To raise the minimum wage so that it's more than $1 more than the hourly I made as a high school lifeguard 20 years ago.
To make it possible for people to raise kids without taking out a second credit card for daycare.
To give people access to affordable health care, without insanely high premiums and deductibles and miles of red tape.
To fight for the miners and their safety, instead of looking out for industry executives.
I'm proud to be [endorsed](https://substack.com/redirect/7509f130-81d1-47b6-b8ec-0e9f531f4124?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the United Mine Workers of America, along with several other unions that fight for workers here in our part of Pennsylvania.
We know we still have work to do. Let's get to it.

clean_body: happy labor day from Hampton Roads | | = Early September in Hampton Roads is about as good as it gets. Happy Labor Day. It's Elaine. I love being out on the Bay this time of year. The heat finally breaks, the days are long...I’ve been all over the world, but there’s nowhere else like it. But a long weekend on the water isn’t in the cards for me this year. There are zero days off from the closest House race in the country, two months out from Election Day. I hope you get to enjoy a well-deserved break today, and take a moment to reflect on the workers who built this country and keep it running every day. clean_body: Peter, I'm going to make a prediction... When the votes are counted this November, the radical left is going to be in a state of total shock. And the political establishment is going to spend weeks trying to explain what hit them. But that only happens if Republicans like you are on record before the Midterms. That is how consequential this moment is. But here is the part the pundits won't tell you. None of that happens automatically. The Democrats are at war with the American people -- open borders, defunding ICE, eliminating voter ID, putting men in women's sports. You name it, they are on the wrong side of it. And yet they are running the most radical, well-funded Senate candidates in states across this country who are counting on Republicans to stay home and let them walk right in. I will not let that happen. And I don't think you will either. I made you a prediction at the beginning of this email. I stand by every word of it. But that prediction is built on one assumption -- that Republicans like you are engaged and ready to fight. That is where your assessment comes in. Sincerely, Newt Gingrich Former Speaker of the House | Paid for by the NRSC. Not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee. |

Friend, This Labor Day, I'm thinking about the people who built this district and rarely get the credit they deserve: the bus operators who get this district to work every morning, the machinists on the shop floor, and the teachers, nurses, and first responders who show up no matter what. **This district runs because working people run it.** So today, while you're grilling with family or taking a well-earned day off, I hope you'll also take some time to celebrate and thank the people who make NJ-09 run. No matter how you're spending today, I hope it's a good one. Happy Labor Day. — Nellie

| Peter,
Louisiana is MAGA's death star. It is the place where they test their most policies before firing them off at the rest of the country.
This summer alone, they canceled an ongoing election under a fake "state of emergency" and eliminated one of our majority-Black Democratic districts.
They passed a bill forcing homeless people into indentured servitude. They criminalized abortion. They deployed the National Guard into our streets. They tortured immigrants at the Winn Correctional Center in North Louisiana.
But a rebellion is brewing in the Bayou.
A catastrophic vulnerability has been found in MAGA's death star, and we are about to blow it wide open. Trump's approval rating in the state is underwater. Voters are fed up with the foreign wars, an economy on the brink of collapse, and National Guard and ICE storm troopers patrolling our own streets.
The rebellion has already struck. On May 16th, Democrats turned out in record numbers and delivered a blow that blindsided MAGA, sinking every single one of Governor Landry's amendments by 20 points or more.
Now Democrat Jamie Davis just outraised MAGA candidate Julia Letlow last fundraising quarter and is statistically tied with her in the latest poll on the U.S. Senate race.
Losing Louisiana would be a catastrophic defeat for MAGA in the very state they built as their death star. And winning this Senate seat could all but guarantee Democrats flip the chamber. That is a move that could save the republic.
We need every Democrat to rally to this cause. We might not get another shot at an upset like this. Prior to running for office, I was an organizer. I saw too many cases of people working two jobs and still struggling to afford the cost of living in the city they grew up in. **It's their voices that I carry with me in the halls of Congress.**

I have spent my life fighting for justice, opportunity, and working people. That means:
* Creating good-paying union jobs through investments in infrastructure, clean energy, and transportation and protecting the right to organize;
* Lowering costs for working families by protecting access to affordable housing, healthcare, and child care;
* Fighting for Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid while working to expand affordable, high-quality healthcare;
* Championing fair wages, safe workplaces, and retirement security for every worker.

# MEDIA ADVISORY

**PRESS ADVISORY: LILY TANG WILLIAMS TO VISIT NH-02 POLLING LOCATIONS ON PRIMARY DAY**

WEARE, N.H. — Republican congressional candidate Lily Tang Williams will visit polling locations across New Hampshire’s 2nd Congressional District Tuesday as she enters the State Primary with overwhelming grassroots support and momentum from Republicans across the district. Williams will greet voters, thank supporters and volunteers, and be available for media interviews at each stop. **PRIMARY DAY SCHEDULE** 11:30–12 PM — WEARE _(Lily Tang Williams votes in her hometown)_ Weare Middle School | 16 East Rd. 1:00–1:20 PM — RINDGE Rindge Memorial School | 58 School St. 2:00–2:30 PM — BROOKLINE Capt. Samuel Douglass Academy | 24 Townsend Hill Rd. 3:00–3:30 PM — NASHUA Ward 1, Broad Street Elementary School | 390 Broad St. 4:30–5:00 PM — WINDHAM Windham High School | 64 London Bridge Rd. **_Members of the press interested in coordinating an interview should contact the campaign. Email Todd@Ascent-Strategic.com with a call-back phone number._**

**About Lily Tang Williams**
Born in China just before Mao’s Cultural Revolution to working-class parents, Lily Tang Williams immigrated to the United States with nothing and built a life as an entrepreneur, educator, and community leader in Weare, NH. A living embodiment of the American Dream, she brings a uniquely powerful perspective to the fight for freedom and limited government.

In 2024, Williams won the Republican nomination and captured 47% of the general election vote against current incumbent Maggie Goodlander — coming closer than any Republican has in more than a decade to flipping NH-02. She is back and running stronger than ever in 2026.

name: Elissa Slotkin
subject: A note from me on Labor Day
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELISSA SLOTKIN FOR MICHIGAN
body:
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2500%2E135344%2EdCsc5r)

Happy Labor Day! As the summer unofficially comes to a close and families settle back into school routines, we take a full day to honor workers, unions, and labor leaders for all their contributions to our country.
Nowhere is that contribution more strongly felt than Michigan — the birthplace of the middle class. We literally invented the concept that if you work on an assembly line, you can afford the vehicle that you built. And organized labor was the tip of the spear.
During my first 19 months as a U.S. Senator, I’ve had the privilege of meeting with labor leaders in Michigan, DC, and across the country. Some of the events from the past 19 months include...
With the International Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail and Transportation (SMART) Workers' at their conference in Chicago.
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/4434?t=2&akid=2500%2E135344%2EdCsc5r)
At the North America's Building Trades Unions (NABTU) at their annual meeting
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/4435?t=3&akid=2500%2E135344%2EdCsc5r)
Of course, with the UAW
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/4436?t=4&akid=2500%2E135344%2EdCsc5r)
With my old friends at IBEW
And new friends in Pittsburgh at the Steelworkers Allegheny/Fayette Central Labor Council’s annual dinner
[](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/4437?t=5&akid=2500%2E135344%2EdCsc5r)
... just to name a few!
Every time, whether I am with a small roundtable or a packed ballroom, I hear about the pride that union workers have in their craft and the determination they have to continue to advocate for fair wages and safe conditions. I am proud to stand with my union brothers and sisters everywhere.
We still have work to do to ensure workers are treated with dignity and respect, and are able to share in the value – financial and otherwise – that their work is producing. Thanks for being a part of that fight.
Thank you,
Elissa

subject: A trucker, a secretary, and me

body:
Hard work helped get me and others where we are today. Let's work now to make sure it does the same for the next generation

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mikevansomeren/a-trucker-a-secretary-and-me?e=356c0699dd)

| |

Happy Labor Day:Like a lot of people, for most of my life Labor Day was another holiday, a Monday off and a good excuse to grill, have a beer, and spend time with family and friends.But as I get older, I think more about what Labor Day really means. My dad drove truck. My mom was a secretary. They worked hard, and I saw what that work provided for our family: a home where I felt safe, where I knew I belonged, and where I could always come back.They also taught me that hard work could open doors.That lesson was one I learned over and over again. I started playing football in middle school, eventually earned the chance to attend college and play at the University of Wisconsin, something I’d never imagined for myself. I carried the work ethic I learned there into law school and, ultimately, into my career.Hard work has given me opportunities I never could have imagined growing up.But on this Labor Day, I don’t know that someone starting out today can follow the same path. It would certainly be harder.
Too many people are working just as hard, sometimes harder, and still can't afford the home, education, healthcare, or basic security that previous generations were able to afford through their work.**I think hard work should still lead somewhere.** That's one of the biggest reasons I'm running for State Senate. I want Wisconsin to reward the employee who works hard, the small business owner who takes a risk, and the family simply trying to build a secure life. If you believe in that Wisconsin too, [**check out my website**](https://us.list-manage.com/1D34Vs9mRsc?e=356c0699dd&c2id=11eeae80ab477324908aa52e5044688f)**to learn more about what we can do together.** Happy Labor Day,Mike

clean_body: Hard work helped get me and others where we are today. Let's work now to make sure it does the same for the next generation | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | If you believe you’ve received this message in error, or if you’d like to unsubscribe from this list, . | | Happy Labor Day:Like a lot of people, for most of my life Labor Day was another holiday, a Monday off and a good excuse to grill, have a beer, and spend time with family and friends.But as I get older, I think more about what Labor Day really means. My dad drove truck. My mom was a secretary. They worked hard, and I saw what that work provided for our family: a home where I felt safe, where I knew I belonged, and where I could always come back.They also taught me that hard work could open doors.That lesson was one I learned over and over again. I started playing football in middle school, eventually earned the chance to attend college and play at the University of Wisconsin, something I’d never imagined for myself. I carried the work ethic I learned there into law school and, ultimately, into my career.Hard work has given me opportunities I never could have imagined growing up.But on this Labor Day, I don’t know that someone starting out today can follow the same path. It would certainly be harder. Too many people are working just as hard, sometimes harder, and still can't afford the home, education, healthcare, or basic security that previous generations were able to afford through their work.I think hard work should still lead somewhere. That's one of the biggest reasons I'm running for State Senate. I want Wisconsin to reward the employee who works hard, the small business owner who takes a risk, and the family simply trying to build a secure life. If you believe in that Wisconsin too, learn more about what we can do together. Happy Labor Day,Mike | | Want to know more? Want to help elect people that actually want to work for you? Labor Day exists because workers fought for it — and our candidates are continuing on the legacy of that fight.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260907-1&t=1&akid=3971%2E587540%2EJUewKb)
Peter,
Labor Day exists because workers fought for it, often risking their lives to make change.
It was the labor movement that won us the 8 hour workday, child labor laws, the right to strike, and safe working conditions. **None of that was handed to working people — it was organized, marched for, and won.**
We celebrate that legacy today and the labor movement that made it all possible.
The fights over workers rights and protections are still ongoing, and we’re proud to be backing several bold leaders who are leading the charge on the issues that matter most to working people.
**Claire Valdez** has always been a fighter for working people. When she was sworn into the New York State Assembly, she put her hand on a copy of No Shortcuts, by the game-changing union organizer, Jane McAlevey.
Before she was ever in office, she organized her coworkers through UAW Local 2110, served on the bargaining committee, and was elected Unit Chair to represent 500 workers. She stood in solidarity with workers time and time again — even taking three trains, a ferry, and a bus to Woodside to stand with Amazon workers on the picket line.
**Donavan McKinney** spent years as Political and Coalition Director for SEIU Healthcare Michigan. He led statewide coalition work organizing for better wages and stronger workplace protections.
As a high schooler, **Christian Phelps** organized walkouts against Wisconsin Governor Scott Walker’s law that stripped public sector unions of their collective bargaining rights. He later became a union member himself, working as a special education professional and joining Madison Teachers Inc.
**Randy Villegas** grew up in a working class family in Bakersfield. As a school board trustee, he banned the use of RoundUp on school property to protect students and the workers who maintained the school grounds.
These are just a few of our endorsed candidates that have stood in solidarity with working people, and they’re exactly the kind of leaders we desperately need more of.
**With less than 60 days left until Election Day, the difference between leaders who will fight for working people and one that fights for corporations and billionaires, comes down to who we elect this cycle.**

Thank you,
David Hogg

The debunkers are working overtime on the Somali resettlement story, and their favorite gotcha is a technicality: Obama didn't cut the checks personally. True -- and beside the point. His administration did. The State Department's refugee bureau and Health and Human Services signed the contracts with the nine resettlement NGOs, including the Lutheran agency at the center of this story, and Somali admissions peaked nationally at over 12,000 in fiscal 2016, on his watch. Whether the president signed each grant or a bureaucrat two desks down did, the money came from the same place: us.
And who received it? Not independent charities scraping by on collection plates -- nine government contractors, several of them more than 90 percent federally funded, placing arrivals in cities like Minneapolis, which now hosts the largest Somali community in America. Then came the fraud: federal prosecutors convicted dozens in the Feeding Our Future scheme, more than a quarter-billion dollars stolen from a pandemic meal program meant for hungry children. Nick Shirley did what our legacy press would not -- he went to the daycares, rolled camera, and asked questions. The video had its flaws. The Senate Homeland Security Committee still called him to testify, because underneath his mistakes sits a fraud case no one disputes.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d0cae926-7e09-4e13-963d-8fb8f1272029?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Now here's the part that should trouble every American, whatever your politics: we cannot tell you exactly how much federal money flowed to those NGOs for Somali arrivals. The figure circulating online is $108 million. Maybe it's right. Maybe it's inflated. Nobody can prove it either way, because neither the agencies nor the NGOs publish refugee funding broken out by nationality. That's not a conspiracy theory. That is the transparency gap itself -- a half-century-old federal program, billions in contracts, and no ledger a citizen can open.
So here's the ask, and it's a modest one: itemized, searchable reporting of every resettlement grant. Nationality-level accounting. Open books at the contractors. Audits with clawbacks when fraud is found. If this program is as successful as its defenders insist, they should welcome the sunlight.
Transparency used to be the thing both parties claimed to love. The receipts exist -- every grant, every wire, every dollar is filed somewhere. The question is simply who's allowed to see them. Let's find out who still means it.

| | _With just one day until the primary, I am using each day to discuss an issue I have highlighted on the campaign trail. For Day 1, I am highlighting my plans to make sure that government works for my constituents in New Hampshire._
* * *
Dear David, Most people don’t think about their member of Congress until something has gone wrong. I’ve heard these stories from around the state. A VA disability claim that has been sitting for fourteen months. A Social Security check that stopped showing up. A passport that never arrived before a flight. An IRS letter that doesn’t match what someone owes. **[Every one of these moments is a chance for Congress to show up. And too often, it doesn’t. That’s the reason too many people stop believing the government works for them. I intend to change that. If you’re ready to help me, I’d be honored to have your support today:](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/MgNxGq7ylNuFea9J9SONAw~~/AAUS1hA~/yPKA-uulqSnjG_GJ5uRyVzo88nvJGhaLVLA46hEsSzRinR4g_tIjz_ZhPwxQSUwhDFtLFnb5Td61qrZSXWJ-07_iVgI0CPs3qjcyN3KGtMh5v5_vY0mmDxzODBJyHvvcqLbynXizKB8tpmdl-rR2vvoyPhFSJWUnyNfw9ea2sjJ2giRZ4VnSXEUTKYE_s1J7YKc3429uhZFCFUWVxeIVZAQhcUFozfkq3X6cd71h4Yrkr5og21ZuLkr9xOBCP3S7roF3HxTScO6yaM5Zo1Pcag~~)** | | [DONATE](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/MgNxGq7ylNuFea9J9SONAw~~/AAUS1hA~/yPKA-uulqSnjG_GJ5uRyVzo88nvJGhaLVLA46hEsSzRinR4g_tIjz_ZhPwxQSUwhDFtLFnb5Td61qrZSXWJ-07_iVgI0CPs3qjcyN3KGtMh5v5_vY0mmDxzODBJyHvvcqLbynXizKB8tpmdl-rR2vvoyPhFSJWUnyNfw9ea2sjJ2giRZ4VnSXEUTKYE_s1J7YKc3429uhZFCFUWVxeIVZAQhcUFozfkq3X6cd71h4Yrkr5og21ZuLkr9xOBCP3S7roF3HxTScO6yaM5Zo1Pcag~~)

Senator Hassan's office has returned more than thirty million dollars to New Hampshire families through casework. Veterans getting back benefits they earned, families keeping checks they were owed. That's the floor, not the ceiling.
To make sure I’m keeping our office accountable to people like you, I’ll publish the dollars recovered, the number of cases closed, and the average resolution time on our website every quarter.
There’s a reason that some offices get results and others don’t: it comes down to whether the caseworker understands how the bureaucracy actually works. **That’s why I’ll hire people who do.**
This means a former VA claims examiner on veterans' cases. Someone who worked inside Social Security on disability and overpayment fights. A former immigration paralegal on U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services delays. I’ll hire people who know where cases get stuck, because they’ve been on the other side of the desk.
I will put permanent caseworkers in Conway and on the Seacoast, with Manchester as our hub. Mobile office hours at senior centers, VFW posts, and college campuses. We are going to the Portuguese-speaking community in Manchester, the Indonesian community in Somersworth, and anywhere else people need services in their language, in their neighborhoods.
When a nor'easter hits and people need FEMA assistance, my office is the surge capacity. When ACA enrollment opens, we will be running clinics with local non-profits across the district. When something goes wrong for workers at Portsmouth Naval Shipyard, my staff will be on site the next morning.
**[Every case we close is a step towards something bigger: showing people a government that works for them. So can you help me make government work for people like us and the hundreds of thousands of other constituents I’ll serve in Congress when we win this race?](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/MgNxGq7ylNuFea9J9SONAw~~/AAUS1hA~/yPKA-uulqSnjG_GJ5uRyVzo88nvJGhaLVLA46hEsSzRinR4g_tIjz_ZhPwxQSUwhDFtLFnb5Td61qrZSXWJ-07_iVgI0CPs3qjcyN3KGtMh5v5_vY0mmDxzODBJyHvvcqLbynXizKB8tpmdl-rR2vvoyPhFSJWUnyNfw9ea2sjJ2giRZ4VnSXEUTKYE_s1J7YKc3429uhZFCFUWVxeIVZAQhcUFozfkq3X6cd71h4Yrkr5og21ZuLkr9xOBCP3S7roF3HxTScO6yaM5Zo1Pcag~~)**

Unions are the backbone of Wisconsin and our nation. Without them, the American people would be left vulnerable to the whims of corporations. Coming together as one has given workers better pay, better conditions, and a better life. But Tom Tiffany doesn’t care about workers. He has been pushing this anti-labor agenda for over a decade. body:

Peter, Happy Labor
Day!

Today we’re honoring the workers who keep our communities and country
strong.

The nurses pulling double shifts. The teachers who buy their own classroom
supplies. The line cooks, delivery drivers, and home health aides — the
brothers and sisters we stand shoulder-to-shoulder with in our fight for
justice.

We're where we are because of decades of organizing and hard-fought labor
battles — workers pushing for fair hours, safe conditions, and dignity on
the job. That fight is what won the eight-hour day, weekends, and
workplace protections. None of it was simply handed down.

And now, those rights are under attack.

Trump and his lackeys will do anything to protect their interests —
gutting workplace protections, trying to squash union rights, and handing
corporations and billionaires another payday, all while people are told to
do more with less. Corporate greed and economic inequality are choices.
And working people are the ones paying for them.

We believe in something different. We believe every worker deserves:
dignity on the job, a living wage, workplace protections over corporate
loopholes, and the right to organize and bargain collectively.

Our Squad — Alexandria, Ayanna, Ilhan, and Rashida — is in Congress
standing with workers, calling out corporate greed, and taking on this
administration every time they try to undermine our rights.

Friends, my congresswoman Maggie Goodlander carries the Constitution with her wherever she goes. She carries it as a promise, not a prop. The founders would not be surprised that a president would reach for more power. They expected that. What would stun them is how many in Congress have simply handed theirs over without a fight. **Maggie refuses to. She stands up to power instead of bending to it.** She swore an oath to the Constitution as a Navy officer, and she kept it, saying out loud what every officer knows: our servicemembers follow lawful orders, and lawful orders only. For that, the President threatened her and tried to have her indicted. She did not back down. That is exactly why they are fighting so hard to defeat her. clean_body: | == Friends, my congresswoman Maggie Goodlander carries the Constitution with her wherever she goes. She carries it as a promise, not a prop. The founders would not be surprised that a president would reach for more power. They expected that. What would stun them is how many in Congress have simply handed theirs over without a fight. Maggie refuses to. She stands up to power instead of bending to it. She swore an oath to the Constitution as a Navy officer, and she kept it, saying out loud what every officer knows: our servicemembers follow lawful orders, and lawful orders only. For that, the President threatened her and tried to have her indicted. She did not back down. That is exactly why they are fighting so hard to defeat her. Maggie just launched her re-election campaign, and the money lining up against her could be staggering. body:
All 125 State House seats in Kansas are on the ballot this year.
#
Hi there,
In this year’s midterm election, the Swing Left community is working to help Democrats in Kansas elect a Democratic governor and flip the critical State House seats that are needed to break the GOP supermajority in the chamber and protect a key congressional district.
**Kansas is facing a crossroads this November.** With Democratic Governor Laura Kelly term-limited, Republicans are determined to seize back the governorship and regain absolute control over a state where they already hold a legislative supermajority.
**If Republicans hold their supermajority and win the governor's office, they will have unchecked power to push through an extreme agenda** —including potentially gerrymandering the 3rd Congressional District to eliminate Democratic U.S. Representative Sharice Davids’s seat. We can’t allow that to happen.
That’s why we have a clear strategy: elect Democrat Cindy Holscher as Governor and flip just five seats in the Kansas House to break the veto-proof Republican supermajority.
[](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-states-ks-2026.CAOW8C&refcode=em20260907-2680&t=1&akid=2680%2E1562180%2EEPw_WV)All 125 House seats are on the ballot this year, and just five close districts could determine whether Republicans retain the ability to push forward with a partisan gerrymander and other extreme bills.
Winning those races, alongside keeping a Democrat in the governor’s office, would instead give Kansas Democrats a critical check on Republican power and preserve Rep. Sharice David’s seat in Congress.

name: Wes Moore
subject: A short message in honor of Labor Day:
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1887%2E1086043%2EVuASm4)
Peter, let me be among the first to wish you a very happy Labor Day!
I hope you’ll have a chance to enjoy a restful and safe holiday today alongside family and friends.
Personally, I never let Labor Day pass without reflecting on how unions shaped my life, and the lives of so many others across our state of Maryland.
I come from a strong union family across generations. After my dad died when I was 3, we received critical support from his union.
Growing up in a union household, you learn this first hand: union members and their families represent the very best of Maryland. Our economy simply wouldn’t be where it is today without the accomplishments of the Labor Movement.
Maryland deserves a governor who will champion for the right to paid sick, family and medical leave. Someone who will strengthen collective bargaining rights. That’s why I’m proud that, alongside our partners in organized labor, my administration is working hard to promote work, wages, and wealth. And we’re just getting started.
Unions have stood with me, and I will always stand with them.
Elevate,
Wes

On all these fronts and more, your support will help Landmark Legal Foundation live up to its motto of "Defending Liberty, Fighting Tyranny." Your gift will help Landmark raise the $750,000 necessary to press ahead this year. The good thing about a donation to Landmark is that it 's tax-deductible. name: Sarah McBride
subject: Happy Labor Day!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
Just think: Without the labor movement, we wouldn’t have the weekend, child labor laws, and so much more.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3804%2E21716%2EFS2qX-)
Happy Labor Day!
Today I’m thinking about the hard work labor unions and working people across our country have put in to get us where we are — and about all the work we still need to do to secure a better future.
Just think: Without the labor movement, we wouldn’t have the weekend, child labor laws, and so much more.
I can remember working my first job, where I was part of a group of employees who voted to unionize. That decision led to better pay and benefits almost _immediately_. That experience shaped who I am today and how I lead, because I’ve seen firsthand how the freedom to organize transforms lives and makes our economy fairer.
I’m proud that in the State Senate and now in Congress, I’ve worked hard to support unions and deliver for working families.
But while working people are doing everything they can to get ahead, Donald Trump and Republican politicians are doing everything they can to pull us backward — raising prices, gutting Medicaid, and handing more power to billionaires.
That’s why I promise to keep fighting back and showing up for working people — and I’m so grateful to have you with me in this fight.
In solidarity,
Sarah McBride

| | Friend, Labor Day exists because working people organized, asked for a day of their own, and the country eventually agreed they'd earned it. More than a century later, I think that instinct still holds up. We set aside the first Monday in September to say out loud that the work matters and so do the people doing it. Around here that means the line at the plant in Austin and the shop floor in Owatonna. It also includes the farmers who will be out in the field this week, or the folks who opened their storefronts this morning the same as any other Monday, because when you own the place, there's nobody else to do it. Plenty of people are on the clock today without much notice taken. The nurses working the floor at the hospital and the line crews keeping the power on so the rest of us can grill in the backyard and let the kids wear themselves out until dark.When I'm fighting for our district in Washington, these are the people I'm picturing. They built this part of the state and they keep it running, and they don't spend much time asking for credit.I hope you get a good day out of it, and some time with the people you love.— Brad
