[](https://substack.com/redirect/fefecf6c-0640-4d45-a1b2-69341ec8ca4b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Last time I wrote about [Micron's $50 billion handout and the property tax cap](https://substack.com/redirect/9af8a8e9-feac-4d45-852b-655b86460c45?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
I keep hammering H-1B because it's the one with a name people recognize. It's also the one with the most rules on it: a cap, a lottery, a prevailing wage requirement, a public filing, etc.
But wait, there's more!
F-1 is the student visa. A foreign national gets admitted to an American college, the college certifies his enrollment to the feds, and he's in (we have about a million people here on it right now).
OPT stands for Optional Practical Training. It's basically a work permit that comes with the degree. Graduate, and you can work full time for _any employer_ for 12 months: no lottery, no prevailing wage, no labor certification. If the degree's in a STEM field... _add 24 more months._ Three years of work authorization in the United States, and Congress never voted on it. It came out of a Department of Homeland Security rule in 2008, and the Obama DHS stretched it to its current length in 2016.
CPT is the same idea, moved earlier. Curricular Practical Training lets a student work while he's still enrolled, as long as the school calls the job part of the curriculum. There's a whole industry of "day-one CPT" schools built around this, where a foreign man enrolls, works full time from the first week, and shows up to class once a month on a weekend and the school just signs the paperwork.
American kids can't get on either one because you have to be a foreign national to qualify.
Then there's J-1 for exchange visitors and trainees, L-1 for moving an employee in from a company's own foreign office (no cap, no lottery), and O-1 for "extraordinary ability," which is the workaround of choice for people who miss the H-1B drawing.
An F-1 student is a "nonresident alien" for tax purposes, so neither he nor his employer pays Social Security or Medicare tax on his wages. That's +7.65% off the top for the company. Hire a kid from Nampa at $85,000 and Micron owes about $6,500 a year in payroll tax on him. Hire the OPT graduate at the same salary and it owes zero.
_**Yes, the federal government built a discount into hiring the foreigner over the local.**_
By year three the company enters him in the H-1B lottery and every year on OPT is another ticket. Win, and he's on the H-1B visa, tied to the employer, unlikely to quit, and unlikely to complain because his employer now controls his immigration status. Like an indentured servant. Lose, and there's usually a way to buy more time: get another degree, another OPT clock.
So the sequence runs F-1, then CPT or OPT, then H-1B, then green card sponsorship. Micron didn't invent it, but it runs on it. Those 573 labor condition applications are the back end of a pipeline whose front end is a master's program.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0909dd87-4e94-4188-8122-1b9716292fdc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_Micron Center for Materials Research at Boise State_
Universities like money and foreign students pay full tuition, usually the out-of-state rate. A one-year master's in computer engineering aimed at foreign enrollment is about the most profitable thing a public college can run. At a lot of American schools, about 70% of full-time grad students in computer science and electrical engineering are here on a visa.
It's our own kind of diploma mill, where an entire graduate program exists to sell the work permit, with the degree as packaging.
Texas, California, and New York mastered this grift:
1. The state builds the engineering school with taxpayer money
2. The school fills the master's programs with F-1 students, who pay more
3. The employer down the road hires off OPT because it's cheaper
4. The state's own kids get the undergrad seat, the bill, and a graduate program where the assistantships were spoken for before they applied.

If you want to see what that looks like after twenty years of it, Tyler Oliveira put out a documentary in April:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/2ffbe56c-8cbc-4875-849d-483ff265ca6a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
He walks around Frisco and Argyle asking software engineers how they got here, and he gets the same answer over and over: _student visa, then OPT, then H-1B_. He has another one on [H-1B "ghost offices"](https://substack.com/redirect/d92dc458-7568-4002-b127-d3a80cb44cfd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) too. Those are the staffing firms that sponsor a worker on paper and lease him out to whoever's actually paying.
He didn't find this. It's federal regulation and you can read the rule yourself. That's the part that should bother you. This is a rule, _not law._
Nobody had to break anything.
Now look at Boise State.
Micron's name is on the business building and the materials research center. Idaho taxpayers fund the College of Engineering. So the company that already has a permanent property tax cap and a sales tax exemption also gets a stream of graduates it pays no payroll tax on, produced at a school it doesn't pay for.
That's a fourth subsidy.
And OPT has no floor. H-1B at least has a prevailing wage rule on paper. OPT has a form where the employer writes down a "training plan" and promises the pay is "commensurate." But nobody audits it, there's no requirement the employer tried an American first, and there's no cap on the number.
It's the loosest work authorization in the country and the word "visa" isn't even in the name.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/cbec963e-b01a-48f7-b181-8848b1ca36fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Idaho can't rewrite federal immigration law or change federal rules.
Of course our congressmen could have some sway there, but we know that's not happening with the current guys, busy as they are [pushing illegal immigration](https://substack.com/redirect/398d1421-2b45-45f8-9b29-92ae2b913c68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [trying to merge the US military with Israel](https://substack.com/redirect/c9e2473f-a3e4-4482-97fd-17caf67fcd76?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [making TikTok dance videos](https://substack.com/redirect/23d08774-1ae2-4d39-973a-867dddcaf23d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
The state does have a card to play here though, in theory.
Every Idaho public university that enrolls an F-1 student does it because it applied for and holds the federal certification to do it, and every H-1B it sponsors is a decision its own office makes. Those are state institutions on state money, and the legislature sets the terms of state money. So we could pass a law saying state-funded schools don't certify F-1 enrollment, don't sign CPT or OPT training plans, and don't sponsor H-1B petitions.
It would never get a hearing though.
You know how it works. The men who fund the engineering school and the men who fund the campaigns are, in a lot of cases, the same men. A legislator who took their check in October knows exactly who they answer to in January, and it isn't the guy who voted for them. The lobbyist is in their office every week, picking up the bar tab, the dinner tab, and God knows what else. The voter shows up once every two years and buys nothing.
Guess who they're going to listen to.
If a kid from Delhi wants to build chips in Boise he should come the way people have come here for 200 years: an employer pays him the same as the guy next to him, pays the same taxes on him, and he can quit whenever he wants.
I'll hear that without foreign grad students the engineering programs shrink. Then run them for Idahoans. Boise State exists to educate Idaho's kids. But a grad program that only makes sense if most of the seats go to foreigners is a business the state has no reason to be a part of.
And this isn't only about Micron. It's any company whose engineering seats go to somebody who arrived on a student visa, took the OPT discount, and got parked on H-1B, while the Nampa kid with the same degree from the same school is out bidding against people his employer can hire for less.
We call that a labor market.
It's a rigged one, and we helped rig it.

I want to share with you why I made the decision to run – and to ask for your support as we begin the general election together. Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision.
When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.
Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.
Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.
So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families.
And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don’t even believe us.
They're focused on their own wallets – not ours.
And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.
It’s why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.
I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.
My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning.
But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.
I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future.
**This is going to be the closest and most consequential Senate race this year, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we’ll be able to flip this seat... and that is together.**
So I am asking:
[**Please split a contribution between Sharice Davids and my campaign for the U.S. Senate today before our next deadline. clean_body: | | | | | Senate Republicans recently announced that they have no plans to spend party money to help conservative Ken Paxton win the U.S. Senate race in Texas. "We in the Senate don't have the money budgeted for Texas. We need help from the president," said Senator John Kennedy (R-LA). Republican Leader John Thune (R-SD) later confirmed the plan to abandon Paxton financially and deflected responsibility to the president. "I'm hoping the White House will become engaged; Texas is an incredibly expensive state," Thune said. What makes this so infuriating is that the Senate GOP spent over $100 million attacking Ken Paxton in the Republican primary. They had plenty of money to spend on Texas when they were trying to defeat a conservative, but when it comes to defeating a Marxist like James Talarico, they’ve got nothing. You would think that since they spent so much against the party's eventual nominee, they would feel some obligation to help him now. This race is competitive because they hurt Paxton in the primary. It should be on them, not President Trump, to clean up their mess. You break it, you own it. Sadly, that's not going to happen. You may hear party leaders say they "hope" Ken Paxton wins and they "hope" President Trump helps him, but they have closed their wallets and are quietly rooting for him to lose. They don't want another conservative in the Senate who will hold them accountable, and they would love to tell everyone that Ken Paxton was a bad candidate who cost them the majority, even though they're the ones who kneecapped and left him for dead. TAKE ACTION Conservatives are right to be mad about this, but being mad won't change it. We need to take immediate action. SCF will pay all processing fees and transfer 100% of your contribution directly to his campaign. Nothing will do more to defeat the feckless GOP establishment than electing true conservative fighters to the U.S. Senate. This is how we must respond. We must win even with the odds stacked against us. We do it because it's our legacy. We love this country and don't give up; we don't back down. name: Katie Porter
subject: What I want you to remember this Labor Day
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Truth to Power PAC
body:
We don’t have to put up with a small group of billionaires and corporations running the show.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=41567%2E3422442%2EErYmIf)
Happy Labor Day, Peter!
Today is a chance for us to honor the hardworking people who fought for the protections we rely on—from the 40-hour workweek and the minimum wage to basic workplace safeguards.
We also know we still have a long way to go before our work is finished. For too many families, the promise of the middle class is slipping away. People who work hard and play by the rules shouldn’t have their budgets stretched thin just to afford the basics.
Your job should allow you to put food on the table and keep a roof over your head. We should have affordable child care so young people don’t have to choose between starting a family or having a career. And healthcare must be guaranteed for all, so no one is denied care when they need it.
Here’s what I want you to remember this Labor Day: _we can win these things if we build a movement strong enough to demand them._ We don’t have to put up with a small group of billionaires and corporations running the show. Our government can, and should, work for working people.
This year, I’m focused on electing candidates who will prioritize the needs of working families in Washington. But to help them win, I need you in this fight.
**[Can you donate $5 to help us support candidates who will make life better for working people?](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260907_1_ak.3d-DXJ&refcode=em20260907-41567&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=41567%2E3422442%2EErYmIf)**

Thank you for standing with me,
Katie Porter

Friend, I’m a proud daughter of a union family. **When my dad joined the United Auto Workers (UAW), he ensured we had health insurance for the first time** , and I learned early on that a union job meant good, stable work. [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm381rcfdHkIQD_K7aziRYYN5JnjCSGCZTnsLdyHpqfDBgsDKBnuRmVpzk-9InI23wCizuzlpYl19RSiHFwm_7Jp1XPjJW1PT_5-cEZW9BMZZcBxWiDz8PqhRwBLvYIO68BUpLPBpWR-TW4bBDumB7vmyjuVyT-aDCQiFozGeAn-ba7PIUkwtrjJWvhVazhnmz9BTuzBWFtR3uO7mq4vboLY7K4FoUpY0J1R71O1BmS7DsWmhUxna_m9sbkCmsxdKJxEBfy1qtUdRxWIroqVyia6CsDkjvvJ97FIj9U4kSx2185ERAwWzgUw1icQ-Lp2P2YfWDZFBFISwJERreq-6nZS5/4tu/VTRqHG9mQQ6SCsMeY5q3dQ/h1/h001.fiQ1E-cLl1BATriZbMIVQC1DxEd0vS-KhfPIPMrRYMQ) This Labor Day, I want to lift up the working people and families who show up to work every day to support their households in the face of an economy and tax system that are rigged against them. Prices keep rising on everything from food to housing and healthcare to gas and utility bills. Donald Trump's illegal war of choice is making this even worse. Meanwhile, the Trump administration continues to insulate massive price-gouging corporations from accountability while handing them and their billionaire owners even more tax breaks at our expense. **Together, we're demanding policies that put our communities first — while holding corporations accountable to their employees and everyone they harm.** **[Please add your name to demand Congress pass a worker-first agenda that raises wages, strengthens labor rights, and taxes greedy and exploitative corporations that pay their CEOs hundreds of times more than their workers.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm381rcfdHkIQD_K7aziRYYN5JnjCSGCZTnsLdyHpqfDBgsDKBnuRmVpzk-9InI23wCizuzlpYl19RSiHFwm_7Jp1XPjJW1PT_5-cEZW9BMZZcBxWiDz8PqhRwBLvYIO68BXvPcWm2ePM79Xc_MJ_CDtlXl-_Sy4t2GokW2S7c_b2wbvUcgPoXbsInBsa3ywwIZYItTksUlJ8QnjLGBuaw0HQPXiNKq4O3ErtP-b--wZpBNf8Pv42uUmb7RniZMvpIZhs2umXcpAos_k4KSzW-r6MvQulHURIN-jZ4KR5OpIfuqhYYta4SuE5jkUFiIxAiMcy9Zg9w53lcFJZcyQRFk5O/4tu/VTRqHG9mQQ6SCsMeY5q3dQ/h2/h001.QovKwRhg6bWCl4g0yHKQlDliRo7QwvhLc0m8NSXWk_I)** | [ADD YOUR NAME](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm381rcfdHkIQD_K7aziRYYN5JnjCSGCZTnsLdyHpqfDBgsDKBnuRmVpzk-9InI23wCizuzlpYl19RSiHFwm_7Jp1XPjJW1PT_5-cEZW9BMZZcBxWiDz8PqhRwBLvYIO68BXnSv1VwDMs48YaVrnWOIxHowVuOlOWnAlKWjQR8qGrf6JOw2i_2dp4hr7a0FzUM_7hLab-buhpn6SOrnjRHwqrtQXwRS7DYa0RsnAhnWIzLCy2UZxQyCQr6_4W8MSW5E9F4g8hAv45kiYO2V2W_xFd4o92oN9ntPWLLu39be5TCymofqVgcR8xao-hljkrD8iMsGdrhBOX1y4563NsS0WG/4tu/VTRqHG9mQQ6SCsMeY5q3dQ/h3/h001.hl7sPOyIXiS0D0opY1jluiHKK1VuanxyX775KT7JjZA)

I understand how urgently we need transformative changes, and I stand firmly with workers, the labor movement, and everyday people who are struggling to get by.
**That's why I've introduced the Economic Dignity For All Agenda, which includes:**
* The **_End Child Poverty Act_** , which would provide a universal child benefit of $458 per child, per month, making it easier for working families to afford basic necessities like diapers and childcare, while providing a long-overdue safety net for all our nation’s children
* The **_Baby Bonus Act_** , which would provide every family with $2,000 upon the birth of their child
* The **_BOOST Act_** _(Building Our Opportunities to Survive and Thrive Act)_ , which would provide $250 per month to adults between the ages of 19 to 67 years old, ensuring cash assistance for households at a time when household incomes are not keeping up with rising prices

I've also introduced:
* The **_Tax Excessive CEO Pay Act_** , which would tax corporations if they pay their CEOs over 50 times their median worker pay
* The **_Restaurant Workers Bill of Rights_** , which would end the subminimum wage for tipped workers, which has been stuck at $2.13 an hour for over 30 years
* The **_Stop Price Gouging in Grocery Stores Act_** , which prohibits surveillance pricing in retail food stores, requires food stores to disclose the use of facial recognition technology, bans electronic shelf labels in large retail and grocery stores, and requires the Federal Trade Commission to enforce these bans and hold corporations accountable
* Multiple bills to lower utility prices

And I'm proud to co-sponsor workers’ rights bills such as the _Living Wage for All Act_ ; the _Protecting the Right to Organize (PRO) Act_ ; the _Food Secure Strikers Act_ ; the _Striking and Locked Out Workers Healthcare Protection Act_ ; the _Protected Time Off Act_ ; the _Paycheck Fairness Act_ ; the _Asunción Valdivia Heat Illness, Injury, and Fatality Prevention Act_ ; and the _Tax Fairness for Workers Act_.

An alternative: buy an entire lamb from my farm, butchered and vacuum sealed, for $450. That's about 50 lbs in total: legs roasts, shanks, ribs, loins, various chops, and 20 1lb bags of ground, all for about $9 per pound. You'll need a 2 cubic feet chest freezer, but you'll have lamb for a long while.
I'll even throw in the organs, if you'd like. If you don't eat lamb brain or heart or kidney, your dog definitely will.
Preventing me from selling, and you from purchasing, is of course, the government. I am not United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) and Food and Drug Administration (FDA) certified and approved, and these agencies and their myriad of levels of compliance enforcement only exist to make Doctor Fauci a multimillionaire by forcing a vaccine on you and your family to keep you safe.
To become USDA / FDA certified to sell our lamb directly, it would be close to $1 million in costs: infrastructure, insurance, legal fees, inspections, etc. Now, the math does not math.
At $450 a lamb, I'd need to sell 2223 before I could break even. At our current rate of 90 lambs per year, that's 25 years of leveraged debt.
The work around: I charge $1500 a lamb. Now that is only 667 lambs before break even and keeping our current birth rate of 90 lambs per year, that's 7.5 years of leveraged debt. Certainly better... but who in their right mind would buy a lamb for $1500?
I would have to spend a small fortune on "influencers" who dance around my farm barefoot and tell their followers _" OMG I just found the CUTEST farm, and guys, it's like so, incredible, and their organic, grass-fed, all natural, hypo-allergenic, non-GMO, lamb (cut to a shot of eating with exaggerated eye roll) is AMAZING you guys, you HAVE to try it, use my promo code RIGHT NOW..."_
If we had to have these insufferable idiots "curating content" in our paddocks, my better half would likely run them over with the tractor.

* * *

But that advertising would drive up costs. Next day shipping drives up costs. I could add volume, go from 90 lambs to 200, but I don't have the grazing land so hay and grain purchases would drive up costs... see how this is going?
Right now... in the simplest form... 90 lambs, $450, easy peasy, you give me money, I give you two huge boxes of meat, but for the government.
Until now.
President Trump's **[Executive Order](https://substack.com/redirect/1e085f2c-73e8-4c89-b4a5-6d09fd33c082?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** allowing farmers to process, package, and sell their products, even across state lines, gets the government out of our free and fair exchange. Hence, my fairly viral tweet. You don't want to buy lamb from a small farm like me? That's fine. You're an adult. Don't.
And many people will not.
Many, many people are afraid, grossed out, or don't trust "farmers markets" or small shops. The big stores, the packaged and certified and stamped and labeled foods give them reassurance. Absolutely fine.
But many are not. And many of us who know and trust our neighbors would gladly purchase meat, eggs, milk, butter, cheese, from them.
That is the choice I am pro.
That $1 million in costs to become certified does not make our lambs safer or better, but it does form a barrier to keep me out of the market. It does protect those giant processors and "big meat" who dominate this market. It does keep food prices artificially high, under the guise of "food safety" and prevent you from more affordable options.

## The Capitalist is a reader-supported publication, we exist for you, because of you!

* * *

The greatest American economist, Milton Friedman, **[argued incessantly](https://substack.com/redirect/be47aa82-babe-49d3-9705-3cab14280745?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that a corporation "cannot get a dollar out of your pocket unless you voluntarily pay it over" making it clear that government was a far greater coercive power over your liberty than any big business, and he is right. So, to get around it, big business team up with big government, and now you are forced to spend your money, enriching companies against your will, and usually under the pretext of "health" or "safety" or "the greater good".
**No one lobbies harder for vaccine mandates than the pharmaceutical company who makes the shot. For the safety of the children ...**
**No one lobbies harder to change the building codes that the companies that manufacture the products. For the protection of the children ...**
**No one lobbies harder for your school district to upgrade to new laptops than the company who sells them. For the education of the children ...**
Your elected official should be protecting you from this sort of forced consumerism, and instead they are active participants in it. I did not cross reference the House and Senate Members of the Agriculture Committees who opposed President Trump's order **with campaign contributions from the major meat processors** because I did not want to get depressed. But you know it. I know it. And the saddest part? They know it, too. **They just don 't care.**
We do not have to be victims of market prices, and regulations and government action should facilitate, not impede, the free exchange of goods and services, and in my case, meats and money. It is rare, almost unheard of, almost impossible, to imagine a politician in 2026 saying "let's get the government out of the way and let people buy and sell according to their own free will". Good Lord, it's a 250th Anniversary Miracle. It's like the stuff of Independence. It's the stuff of freedom. It's the ideas that make America great. Again.
My mind is blown. I did not think we would ever see a President embrace this level of freedom ever. Just think a few years ago Joe Biden tried to make the gas stove illegal.
We need to ride this wave while we can, because the next president, Republican maybe but democrat most certainly, will reverse this trend. You think Kamala Harris will let you buy meat directly from a local farmer? You think a President Gavin Newsom allows free exchange of goods and services without government intermediary? The man made the sale of the gas-powered car **[illegal](https://substack.com/redirect/140889df-34b7-4d02-b172-1ca04260b7da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in California starting in a few years.
So, ride this wave while you can. We can win. We can change things. We can claw back our freedom, one issue at a time. One lamb chop at a time.
**Honor and courage.**

Peter,

You hear it every time you turn on the news... _" Donald Trump wants to be King." "Donald Trump is a dictator." "Donald Trump is a Nazi."_

But actually, it's President Trump's leftist foes who are _the true authoritarians_.

These aren't saviors of democracy. _**They 're Marxists**_.
Consider Zohran Mamdani, the newest hero of the Left, who pledged in his inaugural address that he would replace individualism with the "warmth of collectivism."

And Cea Weaver, whom Mamdani appointed to oversee housing in New York, has said she wants to "transition" away from private property.
Increasingly, they proudly call for outright socialism!

**This is an alarming wake-up call. A warning to Americans across the country to fight for our constitutional rights and our free-market system. **

Because if the radical left gets their way, these things will be gone forever...

I'll never stop defending America, our Constitution, our free market economy, and our Judeo-Christian traditions. And I'll never stop calling out the leftists who want to tear our country down.

I know you won't either!

I'm doing everything I can to rally our fellow freedom-lovers to the fight, through my books, my radio show, and my TV show.

_**But one of the most important things I do is work with my colleagues at Landmark Legal Foundation.**_

Landmark is here to protect liberty, property rights, constitutionalism...in other words, what you read in the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution.

Landmark Legal Foundation battles the Left in court. Their top-notch team of lawyers files "friend of the court" briefs to back up major cases against government abuses. These briefs present the strongest possible argument for the constitutional position and **help convince judges to do the right thing.**

My friends at Landmark fight hard to save our country. And now, I hope you'll join their fight.

* They fight desperately to **undermine our election processes** and, if elections go against them, they use the courts to obstruct the policies We the People voted for.

* They**persecute their opponents** , like when the Biden Injustice Department waged relentless lawfare against Trump and his allies.

* They infiltrate our education system, **poisoning the minds of young Americans** to hate their country.

* They seek to **change the nature of our society through illegal immigration,** creating a dependent class of people who will embrace their socialist policies.

_This is what we are up against right now_. A radical Marxist force that stirs up mob violence against law enforcement and outright sedition against a duly elected, pro-American president.

We must not be silent while these leftists destroy our republic from within.

Landmark Legal Foundation helped overturn Chevron, which gave federal administrators power to define the scope of their own authority and impose extreme rules on every aspect of our lives.

Recently, Landmark urged the Supreme Court to overturn Humphrey's Executor, a 1935 precedent that protects federal agency heads from presidential removal, and the Court did so in a 6-3 decision.

**Landmark 's arguments have helped conservatives win other key court cases, such as winning a major victory to defend free and fair elections, scoring a victory in favor of President Trump's immigration policies, and challenging racially gerrymandered congressional districts.**

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: Fighting tooth and nail
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260907-6687-footer&t=1001&akid=6687%2E420207%2EY1sKGb ]Pramila Jayapal

Peter,

Labor Day honors not just workers, but the battles they’ve won.

Without labor unions, we wouldn’t have the weekend, overtime pay,
workplace safety rules, child labor laws, and so much more. Working people
have secured every major labor law in America.

But right now, Donald Trump — aided by Republicans and their billionaire
donors — are working hard to roll back the progress we’ve made.

Just recently, Trump posted that he thinks working people aren’t working
enough:

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260907.Nv4y2f&refcode=em20260907-6687&amount=3&t=1002&akid=6687%2E420207%2EY1sKGb ]A Truth Social post from Donald Trump that says "Too many non-working
holidays in America. It is costing our Country $BILLIONS OF DOLLARS to
keep all of these businesses closed. The workers don't want it either!
Soon we'll end up having a holiday for every once working day of the year.
It must change if we are going to, MAKE AMERICA GREAT AGAIN!"

Mark my words: We will fight tooth and nail not only to defend what we’ve
already won, but to go even further.

Together, we will guarantee every worker in this country the right to join
a union.

Together, we will raise the minimum wage to a living wage.

Together, we will secure paid family and medical leave for every working
person in America.

Every day, I am honored to stand and fight alongside labor. When we stand
together, we have the power to build a workforce that protects, uplifts,
and supports all working people, no matter what.

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260907.Nv4y2f&refcode=em20260907-6687&amount=3&t=1003&akid=6687%2E420207%2EY1sKGb ]If you’re with me, please pitch in $3 or any amount you
can to help me keep up the fight and grow our movement. I don’t take a
dime from corporate PACs — it’s working people like you who make this work
possible.

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260907.Nv4y2f&amount=3&refcode=em20260907-6687&t=1022&akid=6687%2E420207%2EY1sKGb ]Contribute $3

In solidarity,

Pramila Jayapal

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way for us to reach you about opportunities to get involved. If you need to remove yourself from our email list, click here to unsubscribe:

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:

name: Chloe Cole
subject: A doctor said this to my parents. I was in the next room.
body:
I was 12 years old. I was not suicidal. They lied to my parents and nobody stopped them.

I was 12 years old. I was not suicidal. They lied to my parents -- and nobody stopped them.
| | | |
---
| | | Friend, **"Would you rather have a dead daughter or a living son?"** That is what a doctor said to my parents.I was 12 years old.I was in the next room.**I was not suicidal.** I was a confused girl who had started puberty early and felt different from everyone around her. I had older brothers. I didn't fit in with the girls in my class. I didn't know why.I just knew something hurt.But that doctor didn't ask about any of that. She looked at my frightened parents -- two people who loved me more than anything in the world -- and handed them a choice no parent should ever have to make._"A dead daughter. Or a living son."_ My parents chose me.They didn't know the choice wasn't real.**They didn't know they were being lied to.** They didn't know that what happened next would take something from me that no surgery, no hormone, no court verdict can ever give back.
---
[ **Put Me in That Courtroom**](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT2u2zAMgE8jbzZkSZGdwUOBwNvrUBToKNAUYwtPslyJeUVuXzjNCbry5-NH8teH-4AQw75-h0RT4bsr1YHPyLlUCJ63UDmn5wGFdnZKKtvKaysHB8jhi5yBxk8ePfTY0NQP4zhKI5VqtonUAmT15WrRLEpfzILSWqmktMr2RjVhOnnyKod-lLIfOqMvXoMCi4DLfbwIIyFS4a7Q8VhiQNgZ6uc9F6QOc2ritDEfVehvQs1CzbCTz9zFsFDhJ9LOVLpcVqFm3GKmFnOkNtIKsV2AOZLQc82PguQwexL69uPn3OthsEYo--DkEvnwSELfKEGI7-C_FqFvGxQP9dMB_n6nENIBYd2FvuEd4utkDo7iXgLuFHhXMpWT25TJH39CjKHaQRi5nnNe2_F_PuRrUn8DAAD__wPRnug)
---
**At 13, I had my first testosterone injection.** As a result, I will likely have medical complications for the rest of my life.My fertility is still unknown.**At 15, a surgeon at a Kaiser facility removed my breasts.** I was a child. I didn't fully understand what breastfeeding was. I didn't understand what losing that meant for my future.**No one at that facility stopped and asked whether I might change my mind.** A few months after surgery, I started to question everything.A year later, I knew the truth. I was a girl. I had always been a girl.I was a girl who hated puberty and had no one to tell her that was normal.**At 16 -- after the surgery -- I became suicidal.**This was the exact nightmare the doctors told my parents they were preventing.
---
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT2u2zAMgE8jbzZkSZGdwUOBwNvrUBToKNAUYwtPslyJeUVuXzjNCbry5-NH8teH-4AQw75-h0RT4bsr1YHPyLlUCJ63UDmn5wGFdnZKKtvKaysHB8jhi5yBxk8ePfTY0NQP4zhKI5VqtonUAmT15WrRLEpfzILSWqmktMr2RjVhOnnyKod-lLIfOqMvXoMCi4DLfbwIIyFS4a7Q8VhiQNgZ6uc9F6QOc2ritDEfVehvQs1CzbCTz9zFsFDhJ9LOVLpcVqFm3GKmFnOkNtIKsV2AOZLQc82PguQwexL69uPn3OthsEYo--DkEvnwSELfKEGI7-C_FqFvGxQP9dMB_n6nENIBYd2FvuEd4utkDo7iXgLuFHhXMpWT25TJH39CjKHaQRi5nnNe2_F_PuRrUn8DAAD__wPRnug)
---
The doctors who performed those procedures have not once reached out to help me.They called it care.There was no jury. No verdict. No accountability.**Until now.** You knew something was wrong. Maybe you couldn't name it. But when you saw what was being done to children like me, something in you refused to accept it as medicine.**You were right. I am proof of that.****The Center for American Liberty took my case.** Kaiser tried to bury it in secret arbitration. A California appeals court said no. My case goes to open court.On January 30, 2026, the first detransitioner malpractice lawsuit in American history reached a jury. Six ordinary Americans heard the facts.**They sided with a young woman just like me.** My trial is next.**April 5, 2027. Kaiser Foundation Hospitals. A California courtroom.** The doctors who signed off on what was done to me will sit in front of a jury for the first time.**Friend, that jury will be made up of people exactly like you.** People who trusted their instincts. People who looked at what was done to a child and applied common sense and the law.
---
[ **Put Me in That Courtroom**](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT2u2zAMgE8jbzZkSZGdwUOBwNvrUBToKNAUYwtPslyJeUVuXzjNCbry5-NH8teH-4AQw75-h0RT4bsr1YHPyLlUCJ63UDmn5wGFdnZKKtvKaysHB8jhi5yBxk8ePfTY0NQP4zhKI5VqtonUAmT15WrRLEpfzILSWqmktMr2RjVhOnnyKod-lLIfOqMvXoMCi4DLfbwIIyFS4a7Q8VhiQNgZ6uc9F6QOc2ritDEfVehvQs1CzbCTz9zFsFDhJ9LOVLpcVqFm3GKmFnOkNtIKsV2AOZLQc82PguQwexL69uPn3OthsEYo--DkEvnwSELfKEGI7-C_FqFvGxQP9dMB_n6nENIBYd2FvuEd4utkDo7iXgLuFHhXMpWT25TJH39CjKHaQRi5nnNe2_F_PuRrUn8DAAD__wPRnug)
---
Every dollar gets us one step closer to that courtroom.I am not the only one.There are hundreds of us -- young men and women who heard the same things I heard, who trusted the same doctors, who are living with the same consequences. Most of them have never seen the inside of a courtroom. Because the hospitals have a playbook: delay, arbitrate, settle, seal.No jury. No verdict. No accountability.Kaiser quietly stopped performing gender surgeries on patients under 19 in August 2025. They didn't announce a change of heart. They cited "significant risks being created for health systems."Meaning: lawsuits. **Meaning: people like you** , who refused to stay quiet.**That playbook only works if you walk away.** You haven't walked away yet.
---
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT2u2zAMgE8jbzZkSZGdwUOBwNvrUBToKNAUYwtPslyJeUVuXzjNCbry5-NH8teH-4AQw75-h0RT4bsr1YHPyLlUCJ63UDmn5wGFdnZKKtvKaysHB8jhi5yBxk8ePfTY0NQP4zhKI5VqtonUAmT15WrRLEpfzILSWqmktMr2RjVhOnnyKod-lLIfOqMvXoMCi4DLfbwIIyFS4a7Q8VhiQNgZ6uc9F6QOc2ritDEfVehvQs1CzbCTz9zFsFDhJ9LOVLpcVqFm3GKmFnOkNtIKsV2AOZLQc82PguQwexL69uPn3OthsEYo--DkEvnwSELfKEGI7-C_FqFvGxQP9dMB_n6nENIBYd2FvuEd4utkDo7iXgLuFHhXMpWT25TJH39CjKHaQRi5nnNe2_F_PuRrUn8DAAD__wPRnug)
---
Friend, I don't know you personally.But I know something about you. I know that when everyone around you said this was none of your business -- that children's medical decisions weren't yours to question -- something in you refused to accept that.That refusal matters.It matters to me.It matters to every detransitioner who has never seen the inside of a courtroom. It matters to the next confused 12-year-old girl sitting in a waiting room while a doctor tells her parents there is only one way to save her.**You are the reason that story doesn't have to end the way mine did.** You can be the reason I walk into that courtroom on April 5 with the strongest legal team in the country. You can be the reason the doctors who signed off on what was done to me finally face a jury.**You can be the reason the next girl** has someone standing in the way.
---
[ **Put Me in That Courtroom**](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT2u2zAMgE8jbzZkSZGdwUOBwNvrUBToKNAUYwtPslyJeUVuXzjNCbry5-NH8teH-4AQw75-h0RT4bsr1YHPyLlUCJ63UDmn5wGFdnZKKtvKaysHB8jhi5yBxk8ePfTY0NQP4zhKI5VqtonUAmT15WrRLEpfzILSWqmktMr2RjVhOnnyKod-lLIfOqMvXoMCi4DLfbwIIyFS4a7Q8VhiQNgZ6uc9F6QOc2ritDEfVehvQs1CzbCTz9zFsFDhJ9LOVLpcVqFm3GKmFnOkNtIKsV2AOZLQc82PguQwexL69uPn3OthsEYo--DkEvnwSELfKEGI7-C_FqFvGxQP9dMB_n6nENIBYd2FvuEd4utkDo7iXgLuFHhXMpWT25TJH39CjKHaQRi5nnNe2_F_PuRrUn8DAAD__wPRnug)
---
You knew something was wrong.April 5, 2027 is what happens when people like you decide to do something about it.**Thank you for being one of those people.**
---
Chloe ColeOn behalf of the Center for American Liberty
---
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT2u2zAMgE8jbzZkSZGdwUOBwNvrUBToKNAUYwtPslyJeUVuXzjNCbry5-NH8teH-4AQw75-h0RT4bsr1YHPyLlUCJ63UDmn5wGFdnZKKtvKaysHB8jhi5yBxk8ePfTY0NQP4zhKI5VqtonUAmT15WrRLEpfzILSWqmktMr2RjVhOnnyKod-lLIfOqMvXoMCi4DLfbwIIyFS4a7Q8VhiQNgZ6uc9F6QOc2ritDEfVehvQs1CzbCTz9zFsFDhJ9LOVLpcVqFm3GKmFnOkNtIKsV2AOZLQc82PguQwexL69uPn3OthsEYo--DkEvnwSELfKEGI7-C_FqFvGxQP9dMB_n6nENIBYd2FvuEd4utkDo7iXgLuFHhXMpWT25TJH39CjKHaQRi5nnNe2_F_PuRrUn8DAAD__wPRnug)
---
**P.S.** April 5, 2027. That's my trial date against Kaiser Foundation Hospitals. They tried arbitration, delays, sealed records -- every tool in the playbook to keep what they did out of a courtroom. The courts said no. The first detransitioner lawsuit already went to a jury. They sided with a young woman just like me. Now I need to walk in on April 5 with the strongest team possible. Your $100 today goes straight to funding this fight. You've known this was wrong. This is your chance to do something about it.
---
[ **Put Me in That Courtroom**](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckT2u2zAMgE8jbzZkSZGdwUOBwNvrUBToKNAUYwtPslyJeUVuXzjNCbry5-NH8teH-4AQw75-h0RT4bsr1YHPyLlUCJ63UDmn5wGFdnZKKtvKaysHB8jhi5yBxk8ePfTY0NQP4zhKI5VqtonUAmT15WrRLEpfzILSWqmktMr2RjVhOnnyKod-lLIfOqMvXoMCi4DLfbwIIyFS4a7Q8VhiQNgZ6uc9F6QOc2ritDEfVehvQs1CzbCTz9zFsFDhJ9LOVLpcVqFm3GKmFnOkNtIKsV2AOZLQc82PguQwexL69uPn3OthsEYo--DkEvnwSELfKEGI7-C_FqFvGxQP9dMB_n6nENIBYd2FvuEd4utkDo7iXgLuFHhXMpWT25TJH39CjKHaQRi5nnNe2_F_PuRrUn8DAAD__wPRnug)

Speaker Mike Johnson thinks that being gay is the same as bestiality or incest.

**_You read that right_****.** The Speaker of the United States House of Representatives thinks that being gay is the same as sleeping with animals. Or having intimate relations with a family member.

It isn’t just talk, he has committed his life to erasing the LGBTQ. Prior to Congress, Johnson worked directly with a hate-group**to force thousands of teens into dangerous and at-times torturous conversion therapy:**
|
---
| [ ](https://jjajxo.clicks.mlsend2.com/tb/cl/eyJ2Ijoie1wiYVwiOjEyODY4MDcsXCJsXCI6MTk3OTc1NDIwNTYzMzU4ODQ3LFwiclwiOjE5Nzk3NTQ4MjAzMDg4NDQwM30iLCJzIjoiN2FhNDFlMDQzNWE4ZDBjMyJ9)
---
|

He wrote the bylaws for his wife’s religious therapy organization with a singular goal of forcing conversion therapy on _young children_. Among the most extreme methods of conversion therapy is **Electric Shock Aversion Therapy** in which painful electrical shocks are delivered to the private parts or hands while displaying same-sex imagery.
Now in Congress he has written hate into bill after bill at the highest level of our government to further his dangerous radical belief that homosexuality is a choice. He has:
* Voted against banning discrimination against LGBTQ people across our society from jobs and housing and access to lines of credit.

* Voted against federal recognition of same-sex marriage.

* Authored a “Don’t say LGBTQ” bill that would take funding away from schools and libraries if they don’t fall into line.

He has also said that homosexuality _led to the fall of Rome_ and _equated LGBTQ people with pedophiles_. I won’t stand by and let him hurt any more of my LGBTQ+ neighbors.
I’m **Conrad Cable** and I’m the Democrat running for Congress against Speaker Mike Johnson because I’m sick of this violent hate, there is no middle ground on protecting the rights of LGBTQ people to live safe and enriching lives. **

I am in the fight, and I hope you'll join me.

It's Labor Day, which in this country means two things.**One, somebody in your family is overcooking a burger right now**. _**Two, the sprint to the midterms officially starts today, and everything between here and November is going to come at you fast.**_
So here is an accounting.
In the last three weeks, six things ran at Blue Amp that I am genuinely proud of. Every one of them is behind the paywall. Every one of them exists because a few thousand people pay for this, and not one of them exists because an advertiser approved it. Here is what you missed.
#### 1\. Gloria Steinem Died One Signature Short of the ERA | _Cliff Schecter * September 5_
She died at ninety-two and every outlet in America ran the same obituary. Here is what none of them ran: the Equal Rights Amendment has been ratified by thirty-eight states and is still not in the Constitution, and the reasons are a deadline Congress wrote in 1979 and an opinion Trump's Justice Department issued in 2020. Both are fixable. This piece is the how.
## [Gloria Steinem Died One Signature Short of the ERA](https://substack.com/redirect/7fa9d21e-8ece-4d70-b6da-c76ec4c82f0f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

#### 2\. Russia Has 1,000 Ships With No Country | _Lawrence Winnerman * September 6_
There is a fleet of roughly a thousand aging tankers sailing under flags of convenience, owned through shells nobody can trace, and it is dragging anchors across the undersea cables that carry Europe's internet and electricity. Nobody can legally stop them. Worse, nobody seems willing to try. Thirty-five hundred words on the most consequential thing happening at sea, and I have not seen it explained anywhere else this clearly.

#### 4\. **Hunter Biden on His Father 's Health, Recovery, and the Media | **_Cliff Schecter and David Shuster * August 19_
Ninety minutes, no handlers, no ground rules. He draws a distinction about addiction I have never heard anybody make out loud -- not cured, not still an addict, in recovery and permanently vulnerable -- and then explains exactly what that means he can never do again. He walks through the money: his paintings, about two hundred thousand a year, every single buyer hauled before Congress to testify under oath, set against billions in federal contracts going to the current president's family. He says what he actually thinks about Kamala Harris, which he could have skated past and didn't. He did not dodge one question. Not one.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/f83a29bb-a860-4197-8c5f-6238fd53ae4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
#### 5\. Andy Borowitz Has Stopped Pretending to Be Neutral | _Cliff Schecter August 16_
"I am a Democrat. I've never pretended to be both sidesy." Ninety minutes with the man who created Fresh Prince of Bel-Air on the life of a comedy writer, what Fox News actually wanted when they booked him, and why equal-opportunity satire is a lie when one side is doing all the lying.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/6cf2f8c4-1054-4013-9635-c5acba00857a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
#### 6\. **Raskin: Trump Pardoned Him. He Molested a Child. Then He Tried to Buy Silence. |**_Cliff Schecter * September 3_
Congressman Jamie Raskin walks us through _Pardons, Inc._ , his committee's report on how executive clemency became a cash business -- who paid, who got out, and what it cost the people they hurt. The case in that headline is one of them. Raskin has spent a career explaining constitutional machinery to people who would rather not hear it, and he is very good at it, and he is doing it here while fighting cancer. If you want to understand what has actually been sold off in the last two years, start with this hour.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/3e8475fc-8cc0-4aaa-92fb-17014c49f02b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
That is three weeks. Not a year, not a greatest-hits reel. Three weeks.
That is the whole pitch, and it is the only one I have: this is what it looks like when the people reading the thing are the ones paying for it. No network. No billionaire. No sponsor who gets nervous.

clean_body: [] THIS LABOR DAY, WE HONOR THE MEN AND WOMEN WHO BUILT THIS COUNTRY AND THE HARDWORKING RHODE ISLANDERS WHO KEEP IT MOVING EVERY SINGLE DAY. BUT HONORING AMERICAN WORKERS MEANS MORE THAN THANKING THEM. IT MEANS FIGHTING FOR THEIR FUTURE. FOR TOO LONG, WE'VE WATCHED GOOD PAYING JOBS, MANUFACTURING, AND OPPORTUNITY LEAVE OUR COMMUNITIES. I WANT TO BRING THOSE JOBS HOME. THAT MEANS SUPPORTING AMERICAN MANUFACTURING, CUTTING THE COST OF DOING BUSINESS, EXPANDING WORKFORCE AND TRADE OPPORTUNITIES, AND MAKING RHODE ISLAND A PLACE WHERE BUSINESSES CAN GROW, HIRE, AND STAY. THIS ELECTION IS CAPITALISM VERSUS SOCIALISM. SOCIALISM DOES NOT HONOR WORKERS. IT USES THEM. IT GROWS GOVERNMENT, PUNISHES SUCCESS, DRIVES EMPLOYERS OUT, AND LEAVES FAMILIES WITH HIGHER BILLS AND FEWER JOBS. CAPITALISM IS WHAT BUILT THIS COUNTRY — THE RIGHT TO WORK, OWN, HIRE, AND KEEP MORE OF WHAT YOU EARN. I AM RUNNING TO STOP THE SOCIALIST AGENDA IN RHODE ISLAND AND PUT AMERICAN WORKERS FIRST, NOT THE STATE. I KNOW WHAT IT MEANS TO WORK. I WENT FROM CARRYING CONCRETE BAGS AS A LABORER TO BUILDING BUSINESSES AND CREATING JOBS. RHODE ISLANDERS SHOULDN'T HAVE TO LEAVE OUR STATE TO FIND OPPORTUNITY. OUR SONS AND DAUGHTERS SHOULD BE ABLE TO BUILD THEIR FUTURES RIGHT HERE AT HOME. THIS LABOR DAY, I'M FIGHTING FOR THE PEOPLE WHO GET UP EVERY MORNING, PUT IN THE HOURS, PROVIDE FOR THEIR FAMILIES, AND KEEP AMERICA RUNNING. BRING OUR JOBS HOME. PUT RHODE ISLAND FIRST. When I was growing up, I was a poor kid in a town full of poor kids. My family relied on food assistance at times. I distinctly remember when I was 13 years old, we didn’t have heat or running water, and I heard my mother quietly crying to herself, wishing she could do more for us.

After high school, I became a logger like my dad, and his dad, and his dad before him. When a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages, I fought back. A whole bunch of politicians, including then-first-term Senator Susan Collins, promised to listen, but they left us high and dry — and I realized that nothing would change unless there were working-class voices in power.

So I ran for the Maine legislature, where I served 20 years, including six years as the President of the Maine Senate. It’s been the honor of my life to fight for working people.

I drove hours each way between the North Woods and the State Capitol, because that's what the job required. I won those elections in a district that went for Trump by 20 points, because up here, people care less about a label and more about whether you give a damn about their family.

---
|
---
| | Dear Friend,
There is an unholy alliance forming in America that should not be possible.
**On one side stand revolutionary socialists who believe there is no God at all** – and that America will not be free until every trace of its Judeo-Christian foundation is scrubbed out of our schools, our courts, and our public life.
**On the other stand political Islamists who believe their god must rule** every one of those things absolutely, and that no other faith has any rightful claim to exist beside it.
They disagree about the most fundamental question a human being can ask – _and yet they have found each other._
**Because they have found the same enemy.**

| | | Friends, You deserve a raise. This Labor Day, I want to highlight how America built a middle class envied by the rest of the world – and the decades-long erosion of that middle class and the American dream. For generations, when profits went up, paychecks went up too. But starting in the 1980s, productivity gains stopped being shared primarily between workers and the people who ran the company. Paychecks have stagnated relative to the cost of living. American workers are overdue for a raise. Decades overdue. **Today I'm thinking about the people who make this country work.** Not the Wall Street speculators, and not the bots being built to strip every last dime and every last human job from the people whose blood, sweat, and tears keep our communities running. This Labor Day, Americans deserve a raise. The American economy was once the envy of the world, because our middle class was growing bigger and more secure. When productivity went up, the boss and the workforce split the gains. _Then both parties sold out to the idea that wealth trickles down from the top._ It never did, for a reason that is not complicated. A billionaire can only eat so many dinners and drive so many cars. A hundred thousand families with a raise will fill every restaurant and every dealership in this district. Workers are not a cost to be managed. They are the customers. When a lineman in Campbell County gets a raise, that money goes to the grocery store, the mechanic, and the church. When a hedge fund gets a tax break, that money leaves the same day and never comes back. Growth comes from the middle out. Washington has had it backward for forty years, and 90 percent of America's workers and professionals have not seen a real raise in a generation. The people who paid for that mistake are the carpenters and the nurses and the electricians and the delivery drivers. The people who pour the concrete, stock the shelves, wire the buildings, and keep this economy on its feet. The people who have been told, for far too long, to be grateful for whatever scraps those in power see fit to leave them. At a moment when working people have been abandoned by leaders who claim to represent them, leaders who cut taxes for billionaires, gut food assistance and Medicaid, bust unions, and sell out American workers time and again, the labor movement matters more than it ever has. Workplace protections, the 40-hour work week, overtime pay, wage increases, the minimum wage. Name the benefit, and you can bet it exists because working people stood together and demanded it, and risked everything to do it. That history belongs to all of us, and the fight is far from over. I believe in a Virginia and an America where costs come down and wages go up. Where every worker has the right to organize and bargain collectively for what they deserve. Where the people who power our economy are treated with the dignity they have earned, instead of squeezed dry so someone at the top of a tower can add another zero to his net worth. I am proud to stand with our union brothers and sisters in solidarity, and I am honored to have earned the endorsements of SEIU and the Carpenters in this race. I do not take either lightly. Those endorsements represent people who know from hard experience that the fight for a fair economy is personal. It is the difference between a wage you can live on and one you cannot. Between a workplace that respects your dignity and one that does not. Between a retirement you earned and one that got stripped away. **To every worker who has walked a picket line, filed a grievance, or simply shown up and done the work: thank you. Enjoy today. Rest if you can.** The fight continues tomorrow. In solidarity,Tom __

Her Democrat opponent, with the help of the National Democrats, has raised nearly $11 million to try to flip this seat. Hollywood donors and DC insiders think that if they can pour enough money into this race, they can elect the most radical Democrat ever nominated for statewide office in South Carolina. Every attack ad between now and November is designed to convince South Carolina that her Democrat opponent isn’t a radical, paid gun control advocate or a leader of “White Women for Kamala Harris.” Darline’s Democrat opponent opposed South Carolina's law keeping girls' sports for girls. If she’s elected, she’ll back expanding the U.S. Supreme Court. We know better, but right now, Darline doesn’t have the same resources to set the record straight. Darline has already proved she can lead in just a few short months in the Senate, and I know she will continue representing South Carolina with the same purpose and commitment her brother did. South Carolina deserves a senator who has already spent a lifetime proving she will fight for it. | Monday, September 7, 2026| Hormuz Strikes, $4 Gas

5-minute read · 4 stories
Lead Story · The Iran ConflictU.S. STRIKES THREE IRANIAN TANKERS AS PUMP PRICES CROSS $4What's Happening
* U.S. Central Command said American forces struck **three Iranian-linked oil tankers** on Saturday, describing the operation as retaliation for ballistic missile attacks on two U.S. Navy warships.
* CENTCOM said the tanker **M/T Kylo** sank in the Gulf of Oman following the operation. The missile-attack claim and the strike details come from CENTCOM and have not been independently verified.
* CENTCOM also said forces enforcing the maritime blockade have **redirected 92 commercial vessels, disabled three and boarded two** in the Strait of Hormuz.
* Brent crude rose 52 cents to **$96.80 a barrel** late Sunday and WTI rose 66 cents to $92.14, per market data cited by Fox News. Brent closed Friday at $96.28, its highest since July 24.
* AAA put the national average for gasoline at roughly **$4.15 a gallon** on Sunday.
* Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said on Telegram that any attack on Iran's interests "will receive a faster, heavier and more painful response."

The Situation
* Energy Secretary Chris Wright said transit through the strait is "averaging over 9 million barrels a day now," adding that "the United States Navy is winning that battle."
* Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the plan is to render Hormuz a "worthless piece of water" within two years.
* Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., said on NBC's "Meet the Press" that "the blockade was a smart play."
* Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said on X that America "started the war but expects the whole world to pay the bill" — Tehran's characterization, not an established fact.
* Britain's UKMTO kept its Hormuz threat rating at "severe," citing IRGC drone overflights and surveillance of shipping.
* OPEC+ left October output unchanged; its seven core producers next meet Oct. 4.

The PerspectiveThe blockade is doing exactly what it was built to do: squeeze the one revenue stream that keeps the Iranian regime solvent. Tehran's answer so far has been missiles that missed and threats posted to Telegram, which tells you something about the balance of power in that waterway. But Americans are paying part of the bill at the pump, and no administration should pretend otherwise. A pressure campaign is only sustainable if the people funding it are told the truth about the cost and shown a finish line. "A worthless piece of water in two years" may be the right answer for Tehran; families budgeting at $4.15 a gallon deserve an answer for the next two months.[Read the full story at Fox News](https://elink20c.newsletter.joinjustthetruth.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_N8M2yF9-VjcaxkG0L0zQSXT-8CO4jsxzvo9yiBEDZHe_jgJxJkudBF5AHz3OZO7mKH0m92iBMY7K4JqpDMubFu68KhGQRVKkK-JGD81nEEEZsFNuDUW3Jot4kuJ2uHvkC6MViT1rH_DDQ8cUv-X5lBOQJO6axQfnfIZyX_3t6bhL4--02ZGFIplWpmm3gUmt2IsRlmnyYg5qwrjVzEwmrbbnggpDLF-Nutk1IoMYD9xtNpfVX8NgM7YvTj2_tgkkU99TYcG8kH9t6nXzMKbEZnp4nNjOmMd3Owvd_XVwHbspqH3_HAxlEKhhBEYIPDQ990DxNA7Rw0TGeRYiccs7T0Hi0Gpr9CtHLDE1_xlRn9J/4tu/spfj0ja4RsexseTQ5djHaw/h6/h001.uWWWjksRqo6HEJqgihRheRK9x-OfmoLrjzEkEN6ZB4w)

The EconomyAUGUST JOBS REPORT TRIPLES FORECASTS AS ENERGY COSTS BITEWhat's Happening
* The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Friday that the economy added **162,000 payroll jobs in August** , with the unemployment rate holding at **4.1%**.
* Forecasters had expected roughly **55,000** jobs, according to the Washington Examiner — about a third of the actual figure. Consensus estimates circulated in the low-to-mid 50,000s depending on the survey.
* July, first reported as a month of contraction, was **revised upward to a gain of more than 21,000 jobs**. June was also revised higher.
* Dan North, senior economist at Allianz Trade Americas, told the Examiner: "This is what, almost three times expectations?"

The Situation
* The Federal Reserve under Chairman Kevin Warsh has held rates steady at every meeting this year.
* North said the report gives Warsh "the green light" and "should erase any doubts" about a rate _hike_ next month — that is one private economist's read, not a Fed signal.
* Much of the recent price surge traces to higher energy costs from the war with Iran, with intermittent halts to tanker traffic through Hormuz worsening the supply shock.
* Acting Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling wrote in a Fox News op-ed that more than 1 million private-sector jobs have been created since President Trump took office — an administration figure that the op-ed does not source.

The PerspectiveA payroll number that lands at three times the forecast is good news, and it should not be talked down just because it is politically convenient for somebody. The upward revision that turned July's reported contraction into a gain is a reminder that the first print is a draft, not a verdict — a lesson both parties have ignored when the initial number suited them. The harder truth is that a paycheck is only worth what it buys, and right now energy prices are eating into it faster than wages are growing. Job creation is the floor of a good economy, not the ceiling.[Read the full story at the Washington Examiner](https://elink20c.newsletter.joinjustthetruth.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_F0KAElx4yVoiF03sTMUTyWslDrlWqxLOtIy7S3gUPIASD0ELcOiJzMJMqpPrZwVo3QNMntuMNROev-8oqSqdViIhWY5UreuRgPJdIS84KyDd0xdaXd_VfBU8FRNhaUHtKc9e03G8TIUjBxes5nv5MqsrOgmuQQx94oJolX-kAWEipQiYvcdC7A2ILotuZ6jBK69uB74t_NK8SJfOxGJB3w8SCbDI6tqJbQ4K_fMOZfbVi6o4q6I4w3gUPrtYaIYloUSqpYQvIq-EQehN8skQNkjVmHD115SiBR2pmSJ4L6sHuMp_UbhAWF8Qq0pIz8t0m5Nmp2mbQK-gBYcMnrrfIbP3Sk2beVXzWcqoSEJUBO_cAm6D_ucSEoqTONSK_GHdQ/4tu/spfj0ja4RsexseTQ5djHaw/h7/h001.XOpYY8qORLSjipMxE8JIGog_71Ui_bFauCxbieYRis8)

Election IntegrityMAIL-BALLOT FIGHT RETURNS TO THE SUPREME COURT WITH BALLOTS ALREADY MOVINGWhat's Happening
* The administration filed a new Supreme Court appeal Sunday seeking to enforce U.S. Postal Service restrictions on ballot mail as states begin sending ballots for the November midterms. It is the **third time** the administration has asked the Court to intervene in this dispute.
* The filing asks the justices to stay a **preliminary injunction issued Friday** by U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani, which bars USPS from enforcing several ballot-mail requirements for the November elections.
* Solicitor General John Sauer wrote that "ballots have already begun to be mailed in North Carolina," with "Alabama on September 9 and at least five States the week of September 13," adding: "Once those ballot envelopes enter the mailstream, there is no retrieving them."
* Sauer called the rule "a lawful and modest exercise of rulemaking authority delegated by Congress to the Postal Service" that "regulates the U.S. Mail, not federal elections."

The Situation
* The rule would require mailed federal-election ballots to use envelopes bearing the official Election Mail logo, meet automation requirements and carry unique barcodes. States would submit envelope designs for review and provide USPS with information about intended recipients.
* It would **not** let the Postal Service decide voter eligibility or whether any ballot is counted.
* Democratic-led states and voting rights groups argue the changes are unconstitutional. Election officials in several states say there is not enough time to revise their systems before November.
* The Court has previously allowed the plan to proceed but has never ruled on whether the restrictions are lawful.
* Nearly one-third of American voters now cast their ballots by mail.

The PerspectiveBarcodes, standardized envelopes and a real chain of custody are basic housekeeping, and it is fair to ask why a system handling a third of the national vote has gone this long without them. It is also worth being honest about two things. Weak tracking is a vulnerability, and a vulnerability is not the same as proven fraud — no court in this case has been shown evidence of widespread mail-ballot fraud. And the timing is a genuine problem: rewriting ballot-handling rules after envelopes are already in the mail invites the very confusion reformers say they want to prevent. Fix the plumbing in an off year, not in September.[Read the full story at Fox News](https://elink20c.newsletter.joinjustthetruth.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_NRx3TmKyUjNZ_2a-If6mrdMgnqzjaub68X5IYt-gAktY3XevcNW0zJ0zrs8Uuv6E7gMkUU9Uy4KVYbTESVOSnzbF5sIzh9iQsXVH6lD4wiET-n9COcwhcUFnq75mTX8jy0zqQRHZOA3hb308pxrJ5jLlNJoGN9YQgOlxCpM_lp_x_Td6Vka3yKpEh5djA-TNcSeUqTRpKsM48ZOcksySN0uRVWpETtZTEeDkc1HQEhP4JlnKdA9efjdzwZY5JTZWVAoA1-yEiRotp-A9mW0zGZmTpGj_g_NgMHUCQg6VlyrJPL2hzM4XhnGIynQxspl0MlXRWHszHqq0ge5I9WFQX0/4tu/spfj0ja4RsexseTQ5djHaw/h8/h001.oQySieti29I-6FWXXgGX0N0Rmnz6fyophCe7TjoYs8c)

ImmigrationDHS SAYS 380 HAITIANS ARRESTED IN SPRINGFIELD; LOCAL COUNT IS FAR LOWERWhat's Happening
* Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said at a Cincinnati roundtable Friday that ICE has arrested **380 Haitian nationals in Springfield, Ohio**.
* Mullin: "We've made 380 arrests in Springfield. We're going to continue to push. We encourage everybody to go home... If you want to rebuild your country, go back and rebuild it."
* The arrests follow the end of Temporary Protected Status, under which roughly **350,000 Haitians** lost deportation protection and are now considered unlawfully present.
* The 380 figure comes solely from DHS. CENTCOM also said forces enforcing the maritime blockade have redirected 92 commercial vessels, disabled three and boarded two in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude rose 52 cents to $96.80 a barrel late Sunday and WTI rose 66 cents to $92.14, per market data cited by Fox News. Brent closed Friday at $96.28, its highest since July 24. AAA put the national average for gasoline at roughly $4.15 a gallon on Sunday. Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said on Telegram that any attack on Iran's interests "will receive a faster, heavier and more painful response." The Situation Energy Secretary Chris Wright said transit through the strait is "averaging over 9 million barrels a day now," adding that "the United States Navy is winning that battle." Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the plan is to render Hormuz a "worthless piece of water" within two years. Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., said on NBC's "Meet the Press" that "the blockade was a smart play." Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said on X that America "started the war but expects the whole world to pay the bill" — Tehran's characterization, not an established fact. Britain's UKMTO kept its Hormuz threat rating at "severe," citing IRGC drone overflights and surveillance of shipping. OPEC+ left October output unchanged; its seven core producers next meet Oct. 4. The PerspectiveThe blockade is doing exactly what it was built to do: squeeze the one revenue stream that keeps the Iranian regime solvent. Tehran's answer so far has been missiles that missed and threats posted to Telegram, which tells you something about the balance of power in that waterway. A pressure campaign is only sustainable if the people funding it are told the truth about the cost and shown a finish line. Forecasters had expected roughly 55,000 jobs, according to the Washington Examiner — about a third of the actual figure. Consensus estimates circulated in the low-to-mid 50,000s depending on the survey. July, first reported as a month of contraction, was revised upward to a gain of more than 21,000 jobs. June was also revised higher. Dan North, senior economist at Allianz Trade Americas, told the Examiner: "This is what, almost three times expectations?" The Situation The Federal Reserve under Chairman Kevin Warsh has held rates steady at every meeting this year. North said the report gives Warsh "the green light" and "should erase any doubts" about a rate hike next month — that is one private economist's read, not a Fed signal. Much of the recent price surge traces to higher energy costs from the war with Iran, with intermittent halts to tanker traffic through Hormuz worsening the supply shock. Acting Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling wrote in a Fox News op-ed that more than 1 million private-sector jobs have been created since President Trump took office — an administration figure that the op-ed does not source. The upward revision that turned July's reported contraction into a gain is a reminder that the first print is a draft, not a verdict — a lesson both parties have ignored when the initial number suited them. The harder truth is that a paycheck is only worth what it buys, and right now energy prices are eating into it faster than wages are growing. Job creation is the floor of a good economy, not the ceiling. clean_body: Our primary election is tomorrow | | | | Dear David, Happy Labor Day! Today is a day to celebrate the workers and unions who built and sustain this economy and our democracy. Today is significant in another way too: It’s the day before our election! The moment we have worked so hard for has come. Tomorrow, Granite Staters will head to the polls to decide who we want to represent us in Washington. I couldn’t feel more grateful at this moment. Not because we’re going to win this race (which we are!) , but because of what we’ve built together. ~~ From the beginning, I knew that to beat big-money establishment candidates and go to Washington to pass things like Medicare for All and fully funded public schools, we would have to win on the ground. That’s exactly what we’ve done. From a volunteer team of more than 1200 people to the thousands of doors we’ve knocked on and the more than 35,000 postcards we’ve sent to voters, we’ve built a campaign strong enough to demonstrate real power and bring the change that so many of our neighbors are counting on. But that was never something I was going to be able to do on my own. I needed all of you beside me. And when we win tomorrow and in November, we are ALL going to Washington. I am taking your stories, your frustrations, your pain, and your hope with me. ~~ If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: ** | | ~ ~ | ~ | ~~ Thank you for everything you’ve done for us. |
Peter,
The Missouri Supreme Court just ruled that the gerrymandered map that MAGA rushed through at Donald Trump's behest last year must NOT be used for the November midterm election.
The MO GOP tried to force a new map on voters that eliminated one of only two Black Democratic members of Congress, Rep. Emanuel Cleaver. Under the now-suspended MAGA map, Cleaver's Kansas City-area district went from solidly Dem to blood red Republican overnight.
The justices on the MO Supreme Court just struck down the use of those maps after pro-democracy advocates submitted over 300,000 valid signatures to put Trump's illegal map up for a vote on the ballot in November.
MAGA's scheme to steal a seat in Missouri and ignore the will of the people got Trump's attention, who called the ruling "horrible, ridiculous, and unConstitutional" and used the court's ruling as an opportunity to lay the groundwork for federal interference, saying the "Election Process, as usual, is being disturbed in America!"
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Cpc04_Gv6JDVVW9INW28JJS_gGbBbU362Vm4jgMeXh7Orha1FOYF2c9fDoeSMp69g8vH4rE5csC25MDRRvh3pb1jmzQ2z-ojGD-l5U_ZeUA-dDAZzvdMi7Tyvguqt4cw2-Wy3v2nAjN22knxTanGKEf72S0vhkSu657Q_z0imJxv4P_9eL5Vcra0zB_7208iLtN06ZAgpFraS5AcXE2BfCY9xmP5qJNq55UbprVQad4=&c=bZA8UXDwpH59olV-z9TmiVCHz_N_qozgSJvki00noxCLa6T30JxKQg==&ch=OXexekjENmtprkFI-h5spch6p1gqqVslC2f0sDXI4YLFD1l-BLGFhQ==)
---

The court's ruling suspends MAGA's map and orders the state to use the 2022 map for the November election, essentially restoring Rep. Cleaver's district and taking away a seat that MAGA had boasted about stealing since late last year.
But two MAGA extremists, MO's Secretary of State and Attorney General, have already said they will appeal directly to the United States Supreme Court, where it is a coin toss whether the Roberts Court will respect the ruling or interfere on Trump's behalf.
No matter what happens, justice was served in Missouri as the state supreme court justices sided with the people and the law--exactly what we fight for at Defend Our Courts.
This ruling is a perfect example of why the work we do is so crucial. We're working to expand the firewall of state Supreme Courts nationwide and to turn out voters in the states with the House and Senate races that will decide who holds the power to investigate.
But our main job right now is to make this November's blue wave too big to rig.
[Trump is going to try just about anything to cling to power after November. But he can't steal an election that his party loses by historic margins. clean_body: Justice was served in Missouri as the state supreme court justices sided with the people and the law—exactly what we fight for at Defend Our Courts. | | | | | == | Peter, The Missouri Supreme Court just ruled that the gerrymandered map that MAGA rushed through at Donald Trump's behest last year must NOT be used for the November midterm election. The MO GOP tried to force a new map on voters that eliminated one of only two Black Democratic members of Congress, Rep. Emanuel Cleaver. Under the now-suspended MAGA map, Cleaver's Kansas City-area district went from solidly Dem to blood red Republican overnight. The justices on the MO Supreme Court just struck down the use of those maps after pro-democracy advocates submitted over 300,000 valid signatures to put Trump's illegal map up for a vote on the ballot in November. MAGA's scheme to steal a seat in Missouri and ignore the will of the people got Trump's attention, who called the ruling "horrible, ridiculous, and unConstitutional" and used the court's ruling as an opportunity to lay the groundwork for federal interference, saying the "Election Process, as usual, is being disturbed in America!" | == The court's ruling suspends MAGA's map and orders the state to use the 2022 map for the November election, essentially restoring Rep. Cleaver's district and taking away a seat that MAGA had boasted about stealing since late last year. But two MAGA extremists, MO's Secretary of State and Attorney General, have already said they will appeal directly to the United States Supreme Court, where it is a coin toss whether the Roberts Court will respect the ruling or interfere on Trump's behalf. No matter what happens, justice was served in Missouri as the state supreme court justices sided with the people and the law--exactly what we fight for at Defend Our Courts. This ruling is a perfect example of why the work we do is so crucial. We're working to expand the firewall of state Supreme Courts nationwide and to turn out voters in the states with the House and Senate races that will decide who holds the power to investigate. Happy Labor Day! **Today, we honor the workers who built our state — and the unions that fought to make their lives better.** Arizona's labor history runs deeper than most people realize. In 1884, over 300 miners in Tombstone went on strike when mine owners slashed their wages by 25%. In 1917, 5,000 copper workers struck across the state, leading to the infamous Bisbee Deportation, when over 1,200 workers were forcibly removed to New Mexico. These workers understood something that's still true today: When working families organize, they win. That's how unions built the middle class. And that's why we're proud to work alongside unions today to support Arizona families. **But right now, working families are under assault from Trump's anti-worker agenda:**
* **He's gutting Medicaid,** taking healthcare away from hundreds of thousands of Arizonans,
* **He is driving up costs** on everything from groceries to gas,
* He's stripping away safety regulations that protect workers from harmful substances,
* **He's eliminating overtime protections,** cutting paychecks for families who need every dollar,
* **And he's rolling back environmental protections** that keep communities safe.

This isn't just policy — it's personal. When Trump eliminates safety regulations, workers get hurt. When he cuts overtime protections, families lose income. When he gives corporate bad actors a free pass, working people pay the price. **We can’t let this happen. And that's why we're proud to work alongside unions today to support Arizona families. Peter, Happy Labor Day. Today belongs to the good people who keep Texas moving. It belongs to the teacher who gets to the classroom an hour early because a kid might need the extra help. The truck driver watching the sun come up over US-75 with a delivery that has to make it to McKinney on time. It belongs to the steelworkers, plumbers, and pipefitters whose work holds up every building we walk into without a second thought. And the first responders who run toward the emergency when every second counts. This state was raised up by hands that knew a callus, generation after generation, and it still runs on them today. **That has been the Texas way since before any of us were born.**

**By Wendy M. Yurgo**
I have written about death too many times. I don't want to write another column about dead children. I especially don't want to write one about children murdered by the person God entrusted first with protecting them.
But I cannot watch what is happening around the Lindsay Clancy case and stay silent.
Cora was five. Dawson was three. Callan was eight months old.
Their mother killed them.
Those are the facts that should stop us cold. Instead, I've watched hundreds of people gather outside a courthouse dressed in pink to support Lindsay Clancy. I've watched them make hearts with their hands. I've watched her attorney get applauded. I've read post after post full of sympathy and identification that centers almost completely on her suffering while three small children are already dead.
And I keep asking the same question.
Where are the children?
I understand compassion. I understand mental illness. I understand that postpartum psychosis is real and can destroy a person. I understand that criminal responsibility and moral horror aren't always the same legal question. I'm an attorney. I don't need anyone explaining the insanity defense to me.
I'm also a mother.
And three children are dead.
There comes a point where compassion gets so twisted that we lose the innocent. I think we've hit it.
